Further information, such as rationale and implementation instructions, on how to implement the CRF data collection fields and how to map collection variables to tabulation variables.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or the EDC system. This field can be included into the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: For single-site studies, this is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. \n EDC: The subject identifiers may be system-generated. \n This collection variable is typically collected in all collection domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What is the category for the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/produuct]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product] category, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Category" can be included in the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the CMCAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What is the subcategory for the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product] subcategory, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be preprinted on the CRF or screen and prepopulated in the data management system. This is not typically a question to which the site would provide an answer.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether any (concomitant) medications/treatments/therapies/products were taken/given.
Variables.Question Text: Were/Was any (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product] taken?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the subject took any (concomitant) [medication(s)/treatment(s)/therapy(ies)/product(s). If Yes, include the appropriate details where indicated on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to a tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The intent/purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring. It provides verification that all other fields on the CRF were deliberately left blank.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A applicant-defined identifier. This is typically used for preprinted or auto-generated numbers on the CRF, or any other type of identifier that does not already have a defined identifier field.
Variables.Question Text: [Applicant-defined question]
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, applicant may insert instructions to ensure each record has a unique identifier.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. May be used to create RELREC to link this record with a record in another domain.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Because SPID is an applicant-defined identifier, conformance to Question Text or Item Prompt is not applicable. Typically used as an identifier in a data query to communicate clearly to the site the specific record in question or to reconcile concomitant medication/treatment/productrecords with AEs and/or MH. May be used to record preprinted number (e.g. line number, record number) on the CRF. This field may be populated by the applicant's data collection system.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: Reported Name of Drug, Med, or Therapy
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Verbatim medication name of intervention
Variables.Question Text: What was the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product] name/term)?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record only 1 [medication/treatment/therapy/product] per line. Provide the full trade or proprietary name of the [medication/treatment/therapy/product]; otherwise the generic name may be recorded.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: In most cases, the verbatim intervention name will be coded to a standard dictionary (e.g., WHODrug) after data have been collected on the CRF. For the collection of verbatim intervention name, the recommendation is for sites to provide the full trade or proprietary name, which is more exact than the generic. The full trade name provides the base generic and the appropriate salt for that particular drug. In addition, for coding purposes, it helps with ATC selection (e.g., Tylenol with codeine #1 has a different ATC code than Tylenol with codeine #3). This field can be used for either prior or concomitant medication/treatments/products.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication that a specific intervention or a group of interventions is prespecified on a CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: For prespecified interventions, this is a hidden field on a CRF defaulted to "Y", or added during the tabulation dataset creation. If a study collects both prespecified and free-text interventions, the value of CMPRESP should be "Y" for all prespecified interventions and null for interventions reported as free text.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication whether the prespecified medication/treatment/therapy/product (CMTRT) or the group of medications/treatments/therapies/products was administered when information about the occurrence of a specific intervention was solicited.
Variables.Question Text: Did the subject take [prespecified (concomitant) medication/treatment/therapy/product/dose]?; Has the subject taken [prespecified (concomitant) medication/treatment/therapy/product/dose/]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if [specific medication/treatment/product] was taken by checking Yes or No.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. If the question was not asked or answered, populate the tabulation variable CMSTAT with "NOT DONE".
Variables.Implementation Notes: CMOCCUR is used to report the occurrence of a prespecified medication/treatment/product. CMOCCUR is not used for spontaneously free-text reported concomitant medication/treatments/products. The site should be able to indicate that the question was not asked or answered.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Medication ingredients.
Variables.Question Text: What were the active ingredients?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Prior to a subject's clinical visit, remind all subjects to bring all medications bottles, packs etc. they are taking with them to their clinical visit. Record all active ingredient(s) off the intervention label and separate each ingredient with a comma for the name of drug, medication, treatment or product taken. For example, the medication Dolmen, if manufactured in Spain, the active ingredients should be collected as noted below: Active ingredient: Acetylsalicylic Acid, Ascorbic acid, codeine phosphate.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to a tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This may be collected in addition to the medication/treatment/product name. Collecting this provides more detailed information when coding to a medication dictionary like WHODrug Dictionary Enhanced Format C, which codes to the ingredient level for many trade-name medications. For example, depending on the country where it is manufactured, the active ingredients in the medication dolmen may be different: In Spain, acetylsalicylic acid, ascorbic acid, codeine phosphate; in Italy and Czech Republic, tenoxicam; in Estonia and Latvia, dexketoprofen trometamol.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The condition, disease, symptom, or disorder that the concomitant (non-study) medication/treatment/therapy/product was used to address or investigate (e.g., why the medication/treatment/therapy/product was taken or administered).
Variables.Question Text: For what indication was the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product] taken?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the reason the medication was taken based on clinical investigator's evaluation. If taken to treat a condition, and a diagnosis was made, the indication should be the diagnosis. If taken to treat a condition, and no diagnosis was made, the indication should be the signs and symptoms. If taken as prophylaxis, report as "Prophylaxis for " and include a description of the condition(s).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This is not the pharmacological/therapeutic classification of an agent (e.g., antibiotic, analgesic), but rather the reason for its administration to the subject. This additional information is collected on the CRF when applicants want to capture the reason(s) a subject took a medication/treatment/product. This information could be used as deemed appropriate for coding; analysis (e.g., in the classification of medications); reconciling medications/treatments/products taken by a subject with provided medical history; and/or AEs/SAEs, as part of the data clean-up and monitoring process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Identifier for the adverse event that is the indication for this medication/treatment/therapy/product.
Variables.Question Text: What was the identifier for the adverse event(s) for which the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product] was taken?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier of the Adverse Event for which this (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product] was taken.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For tabulation datasets, may be used to create RELREC to link this record with a record in the AE domain.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The intent is to establish a link between the medication/treatment and the AE that was reported. CMAENO can be used to identify a relationship between records in CM dataset and records in the AE dataset.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Identifier for the medical history condition that is the indication for this medication/treatment/therapy/product.
Variables.Question Text: What was the identifier for the medical history event(s) for which the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product] was taken?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier of the medical history event for which this (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product] was taken.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For tabulation datasets, may be used to create RELREC to link this record with a record in the MH domain.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The intent is to establish a link between the medical history condition and the intervention taken for the condition. CMMHNO can be used to identify a relationship between records in the CM dataset and records in the MH dataset.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dose of medication/treatment/product (e.g., --TRT ) given at one time, represented as a numeric value.
Variables.Question Text: What was the individual dose (of the concomitant [medication/treatment/therapy/product] per administration)?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the dose of (concomitant) [medication/treatment/product] taken per administration (e.g., 200).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Used when the dose/amount taken/administered/consumed has only numeric entries. If non-numeric entries are possible, use the collection field CMDSTXT.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dose of medication/treatment/product taken per administration.
Variables.Question Text: What was the individual dose of the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the dose of (concomitant) [medication/treatment/product] taken per administration (e.g., 200).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. Numeric values map to CMDOSE in the tabulation dataset. Non-numeric values (e.g., "200-400") map to CMDOSTXT in the tabulation dataset.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Defining this data collection field as a dose text field allows for flexibility in capturing dose entries as numbers, text, or ranges. The data collected in this text-format field should be separated or mapped to either tabulation CMDOSE if numeric or CMDOSTXT if text.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The total amount of CMTRT taken over a day, using the units in CMDOSU.
Variables.Question Text: What was the total daily dose of the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the total dose of (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product] taken daily.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: For use when only total daily dose is collected on the CRF. For general medications/treatments/produts, it is not recommended to use Total Daily Dose. Instead, this can be calculated from other fields (e.g., Units, Dose, Frequency).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit associated with the concomitant medication/treatment/therapy/product taken (e.g., mg in "2 mg 3 times per day").
Variables.Question Text: What is the unit (for the dose of concomitant [medication/treatment/therapy/product])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the dose unit of the dose of concomitant [medication/treatment/therapy/product] taken (e.g., mg.).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: When applicants collect data for amount of dose taken (i.e., Dose, Total Daily Dose), Unit must be collected as well (if applicable).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The pharmaceutical dosage form in which the CMTRT is physically presented.
Variables.Question Text: What was the dose form of the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the pharmaceutical dosage form (e.g., TABLET CAPSULE, SYRUP) of delivery for the concomitant [medication/treatment/therapy/product] taken.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Some drugs have multiple forms; this field may be needed to code the drug to an ATC level. However, in general, this level of detail should not be necessary except for medications/treatments/products of interest.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The number of doses given/administered/taken during a specific interval.
Variables.Question Text: What was the frequency of the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record how often the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product] was taken (e.g., BID, PRN).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The frequency of the concomitant medication/treatment/product. When collected, the recommendation is to collect dosing information in separate fields (e.g., CMDOSE, CMDOSEU, CMDOSFRQ) for specific and consistent data collection and to enable programmatically using these data.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The route of administration of the concomitant medication/treatment/therapy/product.
Variables.Question Text: What was the route of administration of the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Provide the route of administration for the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product].
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This additional information may be important to collect on the CRF when the applicant wants to capture a medication's/treatment's /product's route of administration, for purposes such as coding; also, the medication/treatment/product may have more than 1 route. Some companies may use route in coding medications/treatments/products, to be able to choose a precise preferred name and ATC code.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The start date is when the concomitant medication/treatment/therapy/product was first taken, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product/dose] start date?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the date the concomitant [medication/treatment/product] was first taken using this format (DD-MON-YYYY). If the subject has been taking the concomitant [medication/treatment/product] for a considerable amount of time prior to the start of the study, it is acceptable to have an incomplete date. Concomitant [medication/treatment/product] taken during the study are expected to have a complete start date. Prior concomitant [medication/treatment/product] that are exclusionary should have both a start and end date.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable CMSTDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The assumption is that applicants should either have a start date or will indicate that the medication, therapy, or product was started before, during, or after the study period. The preferred method is to collect a complete start date. Partial dates (e.g., providing year only) for medications/treatment/product started a considerable amount of time prior to the start of study are acceptable.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The time the concomitant medication/treatment/therapy/product was started, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product/dose] start time?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the time (as complete as possible) that the concomitant [medication/treatment/product] was started.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable CMSTDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Recommend collecting the time a concomitant medication/treatment/product was started only when a protocol or data collection scenarios supports it. Typically, a start time is not collected unless the subject is under the direct care of the site at the time a concomitant medication/treatment/product administered or the subject records the start time in a diary.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Indication the concomitant medication/treatment/therapy/product was given or taken prior to [CMSTTPT] or prior to the date in DM.RFSTDTC.
Variables.Question Text: Was the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product] given/taken prior to [CMSTTPT]?; Was the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product] given/taken prior to study start?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Check if the concomitant [medication/treatment/therapy/product] was started before the study.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. May be used to populate a value into a tabulation relative timing variable such as CMSTRF or CMSTRTPT. When populating CMSTRF, or CMSTRTPT, if the value of the collection field CMPRIOR is "Y" a value from the CDISC CT (STENRF) may be used. When CMPRIOR refers to the Study Reference Period (defined in DM.RFSTDTC to DM.RFENDTC), the tabulation variable CMSTRF should be populated. When CMPRIOR is compared to another timepoint, the tabulation variables CMSTRTPT and CMSTTPT should be used. Note: CMSTRTPT must refer to the time-point anchor described in CMSTTPT.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicants may collect this information rather than start dates.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Indication the concomitant medication/treatment/therapy/product is ongoing when no end date is provided.
Variables.Question Text: Was the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product] ongoing (as of [the study-specific timepoint or period])?
Variables.Prompt: Ongoing (as of [the study-specific timepoint or period])
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the concomitant [medication/treatment/therapy/product] as ongoing if the subject has not stopped taking the concomitant [medication/treatment/therapy/product] at [the timepoint defined by the study]. If the concomitant medication/treatment/therapy/product is ongoing, the end date should be left blank
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. May be used to populate a value into a tabulation relative timing variable (e.g., CMENRF, CMENRTPT). When populating CMENRF, if the value of CMONGO is "Y", the values of "DURING", "AFTER", or "DURING/AFTER" may be used. When populating CMENRTPT, if the value of CMONGO is "Y", the value of "ONGOING" may be used. When CMONGO refers to the Study Reference Period (defined in DM.RFSTDTC to DM.RFENDTC) the tabulation variable CMENRF should be populated. When CMONGO is used in conjunction with another timepoint, the tabulation variables CMENRTPT and CMENTPT should be used. Note: CMENRTPT must refer to a time-point anchor described in CMENTPT.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This box should be checked to indicate that the concomitant medication/treatment/product has not stopped at the time of data collection. It is expected that every recorded medication/treatment/product should have either an end date or be checked as ongoing, but not both. However, in cases where ongoing concomitant medications/treatments/products are not permitted, it may not be necessary to include an Ongoing field in the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date that the subject ended/stopped taking the concomitant medication/treatment/therapy/product, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product/dose] end date?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the date the concomitant [medication/treatment/product] was stopped using this format (DD-MON-YYYY). If the subject has not stopped taking the concomitant [medication/treatment/product] leave this field blank.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected END DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable CMENDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The assumption is that applicants should either have an end date or will indicate that the medication, therapy, or product was ongoing at the time of collection or at the end of the study. However, in cases where the end date can be determined from dates collected elsewhere in the CRF it is not necessary to include an End Date field on the CRF. For example, if all concomitant medications/treatments/products are administered only once during a trial, the end date will be the same as the start date.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The time when the subject ended/stopped taking the concomitant medication/treatment/therapy/product, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the [medication/treatment/therapy/product/dose] end time?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the time (as complete as possible) that the concomitant medication/treatment/product was stopped.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected END DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable CMENDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Recommend collecting the time a concomitant medication,treatment, product was ended only when a protocol or data collection scenario requires it or the subject records the end time in a diary. Typically, an end time is not collected unless the subject is under the direct care of the site at the time a concomitant medication/treatment/product is stopped.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The reason the Intervention was discontinued.
Variables.Question Text: What was the reason the (concomitant) [medication/treatment/therapy/product/--TRT] was [discontinued/stopped/ended]?
Variables.Prompt: Reason for discontinuation of concomitant medication/treatment/therapy/product.
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the reason the concomitant medication/treatment/product was stopped.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although frequently used for prior meds, this can be used for any intervention at any timepoint. \n When the dosing is recorded over multiple successive records, this variable is applicable only for the (chronologically) last record for the intervention.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary or applicant-defined standardized text description of the topic variable, CMTRT, or the modified topic variable (CMMODIFY), if applicable.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. Applicants will populate this through the coding process. Equivalent to the generic drug name in published (e.g., WHODrug, SNOMED, ICD9) or applicant-defined dictionaries.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The class for the intervention (often obtained from a coding dictionary).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. Applicants will populate this through the coding process. This would generally be the class code used for analysis.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The assigned dictionary code for the class for the intervention.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. Applicants will populate this through the coding process. This would generally be the class code used for analysis.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Dictionary text description of the first level of hierarchy within the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification system; indicates the anatomical main group.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPCM dataset as the value of SUPPCM.QVAL where SUPPCM.QNAM="CMATC1" and SUPPCM.QLABEL="ATC Level 1 Description".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. This is populated through the applicant's coding process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Dictionary code denoting the first level of hierarchy within the ATC classification system; indicates the anatomical main group.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPCM dataset as the value of SUPPCM.QVAL where SUPPCM.QNAM ="MATC1CD" and SUPPCM.QLABEL="ATC Level 1 Code".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. This is populated through the applicant's coding process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Dictionary text description for the second level of hierarchy within the ATC classification system; indicates the therapeutic main group.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPCM dataset as the value of SUPPCM.QVAL where SUPPCM.QNAM="CMATC2" and SUPPCM.QLABEL="ATC Level 2 Description".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. This is populated through the applicant's coding process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Dictionary code denoting the second level of hierarchy within the ATC classification system; indicates the therapeutic main group.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPCM dataset as the value of SUPPCM.QVAL where SUPPCM.QNAM="CMATC2CD" and SUPPCM.QLABEL="ATC Level 2 Code".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. This is populated through the applicant's coding process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Dictionary text description of the third level of hierarchy within the ATC classification system; indicates the therapeutic/pharmacological subgroup.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPCM dataset as the value of SUPPCM.QVAL where SUPPCM.QNAM="CMATC3" and SUPPCM.QLABEL="ATC Level 3 Description".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. This is populated through the applicant's coding process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Dictionary code denoting the third level of hierarchy within the ATC classification system; indicates the therapeutic/pharmacological subgroup.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPCM dataset as the value of SUPPCM.QVAL where SUPPCM.QNAM="CMATC3CD" and SUPPCM.QLABEL="ATC Level 3 Code".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. This is populated through the applicant's coding process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Dictionary text description of the fourth level of hierarchy within the ATC classification system; indicates the chemical/therapeutic/pharmacological subgroup.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPCM dataset as the value of SUPPCM.QVAL where SUPPCM.QNAM="CMATC4" and SUPPCM.QLABEL="ATC Level 4 Description".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. This is populated through the applicant's coding process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Dictionary code denoting the fourth level of hierarchy within the ATC classification system; indicates the chemical/therapeutic/pharmacological subgroup.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPCM dataset as the value of SUPPCM.QVAL where SUPPCM.QNAM="CMATC4CD" and SUPPCM.QLABEL="ATC Level 4 Code".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. This is populated through the applicant's coding process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Dictionary text description of the fifth level of hierarchy within the ATC classification system; indicates the chemical substance.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPCM dataset as the value of SUPPCM.QVAL where SUPPCM.QNAM="CMATC5" and SUPPCM.QLABEL="ATC Level 5 Description".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. This is populated through the applicant's coding process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Dictionary code denoting the fifth level of hierarchy within the ATC classification system; indicates the chemical substance.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPCM dataset as the value of SUPPCM.QVAL where SUPPCM.QNAM="CMATC5CD" and SUPPCM.QLABEL="ATC Level 5 Code".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. This is populated through the applicant's coding process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included in the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. \n EDC: The subject identifiers may be system generated. \n This collection variable is typically collected in all domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Name of the trial epoch with which this element of the arm is associated.
Variables.Question Text: What is the trial epoch?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: [protocol specific]
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: If the same information is collected more than once in different periods/parts of a study (e.g., Disposition), EPOCH may be needed to differentiate them. Typically, the trial epoch will be preprinted on the CRF as the title of the page.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether the subject used the study product.
Variables.Question Text: Were any[study product/dose] taken?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the subject used any study products. If Yes, include the appropriate details where indicated.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to a tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The intent/purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring. It provides verification that all other fields on the CRF were deliberately left blank. The ECYN is meant to indicate that the exposure as collected form should be completed or inserted into the case book. ECOCCUR would be used when the actual product name is preprinted on the CRF. While these might be equivalent in a single-product study, there are differences in how they would be used in most trials. Therefore, it does not map into the tabulation variable ECOCCUR; ECOCCUR indicates whether the subject actually used study product. If actual data is available (ECYN ="Y"), ECOCCUR may be populated based on whether subject was actually used study product.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What is the category of the [study product/dose]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the study product category, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, and not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Category" can be included as the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the ECCAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What is the subcategory of the [study product/dose]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the study product subcategory, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be preprinted on the CRF or screen and prepopulated in the data management system. This is not typically a question to which the site would provide an answer. ECSCAT can only be used if there is an ECCAT and it must be a subcategorization of ECCAT.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Name of the study product.
Variables.Question Text: What was the [study product] name?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the name of study product.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: ECTRT is the name of the product.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication that a specific intervention or a group of interventions is prespecified on a CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: For prespecified interventions, a hidden field on a CRF defaulted to "Y", or added during the tabulation dataset creation. If a study collects both prespecified and free-text interventions, the value of ECPRESP should be "Y" for all prespecified interventions and null for interventions reported as free text.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication whether the study product was used when information about the occurrence of a specific intervention was solicited.
Variables.Question Text: Was [study product/dose] used?; Has the subject taken [study product/dose]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the subject used study product. If Yes, include the appropriate details where indicated.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. Not applicable when ECMOOD is "Scheduled".
Variables.Implementation Notes: ECOCCUR is used to indicate whether the subject actually used study product. ECOCCUR should not be used to indicate that the question was not asked or answered.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An explanation for why a scheduled study product administration did or did not occur.
Variables.Question Text: What was the reason that the [study product/dose] was (not) used?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate why the study product was or was not used.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This information could be represented in a SUPPEC dataset as the value of SUPPEC.QVAL where SUPPEC.QNAM="ECREASOC" and SUPPEC.QLABEL ="Reason for Occur Value".
Variables.Implementation Notes: The reason the study product was or was not taken may be chosen from an applicant-defined codelist or entered as free text. When --REASOC is used, --OCCUR must also be populated in the tabulation dataset with a value of "Y" or "N".

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Mode or condition of the record specifying whether the intervention (activity) is intended to happen or has happened.
Variables.Question Text: Does this record describe scheduled [study product/dose] or used [study product/dose]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if this record has happened or is intended to happen.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. When implemented, ECMOOD must be populated for all records.
Variables.Implementation Notes: "SCHEDULED" is for collected subject-level intended dose records. "PERFORMED" is for collected subject-level actual dose records. "Planned" or "Scheduled" can be preprinted as the CRF name or section header, as applicable. If collecting both the scheduled and performed dosing in the same horizontal record, the applicant may choose to append "_SCHEDULED" to the ECDOSE/ECDOSTXT variable name to delineate the scheduled dose from the performed dose. The performed dose would just be collected with ECDOSE/ECDOSTXT and ECDOSU.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An internal or external identifier (e.g., kit number, bottle label, vial identifier).
Variables.Question Text: What is the [study product/dose] label identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record product label identifier.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This packaging identifier (e.g., kit number, bottle label, vial identifier) may be collected in different ways (e.g., affixing label onto CRF, scanning a bar code). For some study dosing regimens that require greater granularity for product identifiers, applicants may need to use additional variables.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Lot number of the ECTRT product.
Variables.Question Text: What was the lot number of the [study product/dose] used?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the lot number that appears on the container holding the study product.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The lot number identifies the manufacturing batch of the study product. In open-label studies, the reference number on the study product container may represent an actual lot number and should be represented using ECLOT. This variable may be populated during the process of creating the tabulation datasets. Do not collect other identification variables in this field.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dosage form in which the ECTRT is physically presented.
Variables.Question Text: What was the dose form of the [studyproduct /dose]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the dose form (e.g., SOLUTION, TABLET, LOTION) or enter the appropriate code from the code list.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This must be collected if it cannot be determined from other sources or if there are multiple options for the same study product.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The start date of study product, intended or actual, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the ([intended/planned/actual]) ([study product/dose]) (start) date?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the start date of the study product administration using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable ECSTDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Date when constant dosing interval of the study product started or single administration occurred. When collecting the date for an individual dose, the word "start" may be omitted from the Question Text and Prompt. When ECMOOD is collected and ECMOOD is "SCHEDULED", use "intended" in the question text and prompt. When ECMOOD is collected and ECMOOD is "PERFORMED", use "actual" in the question text and prompt.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The start time of study product, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the ([intended/planned/actual]) ([study product/dose]) (start) time?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the start time (as complete as possible) when administration of study product started.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable ECSTDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Recommend collecting the time a product was started only when a protocol or data collection scenarios requires it. When collecting the time for an individual dose, the word "start" may be omitted from the question text and prompt.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The end date of study product, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the ([intended/planned/actual]) ([study product/dose]) (end) date?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the end date of the study product use using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected END DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable ECENDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Date when study product period stopped. If start date and end date are not expected to be the same date, the collection of the end date is required. If the study design indicates that the start and end are on the same day, the collection of the end date is not required because it can be assigned to be equal to the start date.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The end time of study product use, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the ([intended/planned/actual]) ([study product/dose]) (end) time?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the time, (as complete as possible) when study product use stopped (e.g., for infusions this is the time when the infusion ended).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected END DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable ECENDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Recommend collecting the time a med was ended when a protocol or data collection scenarios requires it. For infusions, the end time of the infusion is typically needed.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dose of study product taken (per administration).
Variables.Question Text: What was the dose (per administration) (of [study product/dose])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the dose or amount of study product that was used to/taken by the subject in the period recorded; from the start date/time to the end date/time inclusive.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. The data collected in this dose text-format field should be mapped to either ECDOSE if numeric or ECDOSTXT if text.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Dose or amount taken for single use of study product or per constant use interval recorded. Dose must be collected if it cannot be determined via other methods (e.g., from diary data, procuct accountability data, protocol). Care should be taken when mapping ECDSTXT. The data collected in this dose text-format field should be separated or mapped to either ECDOSE if numeric or ECDOSTXT if text.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit for intended dose (per administration) for ECDOSE, ECDOSTOT, or ECDOSTXT.
Variables.Question Text: What were the units for the dose?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the unit of dose or amount taken per period recorded (e.g., ng, mg, mg/kg).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Unit of dose or amount taken per constant dosing interval recorded. Dose unit must be collected if it cannot be determined via other methods (e.g., from protocol, randomization data). The unit should be preprinted on the CRF or a field provided on the CRF to capture it. A CDASH Subset Controlled Terminology Codelist Name is available for dose and volume units. In blinded trials, the collected unit may be tablet, capsule, etc., since the actual unit is also blinded.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The number of doses taken during a specific interval.
Variables.Question Text: What was the frequency of [study product/dose] dosing?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the frequency the study product was used for a defined period of time (e.g., BID, QID, TID).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This may be collected if it cannot be determined from other sources or if there are multiple options. When possible, the options for dose/amount frequency are preprinted on the CRF. When collected, the recommendation is to collect dosing information in separate fields (e.g., ECDOSE, ECDOSEU, ECDOSFRQ) for specific and consistent data collection and to enable programmatically using these data.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The route of administration of the study product
Variables.Question Text: What was the route of use (of the [study product/dose])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the route of administration (e.g., IV, ORAL, TRANSDERMAL) or enter the appropriate code from the code list.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This may be collected if it cannot be determined via other methods (e.g., from protocol) or if there are multiple options.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether the dose was adjusted.
Variables.Question Text: Was the dose adjusted?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Select either Yes or No to indicate whether there was a change in dosing.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: When ECADJ is collected, does not map to a tabulation variable. When ECADJ is not collected, applicant may represent this variable in SUPPEC.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Typically, the intent/purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring, as it provides a definitive response regarding any dose changes. It provides verification that the associated field on the CRF (ECADJ) was deliberately left blank. However, the applicant may collect whether the dose was adjusted, without collecting the reason for the change. When using ECMOOD, this field should not be used.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Description of or explanation for why a dose of the study product was adjusted.
Variables.Question Text: What was the reason the dose was adjusted?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If there was a change in dosing, record the reason for change.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Captures the reason the dose was changed or modified. The reason may be chosen from an applicant-defined list (e.g., adverse event, insufficient response) or entered as free text. May be used for variations from protocol-specified doses, or changes from expected doses. Used only when an adjustment is represented in EX dataset.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether the exposure was interrupted.
Variables.Question Text: Was the [(study) product/dose] interrupted?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record if there was an interruption in the study product use or dosing.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to a tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The intent/purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring when the actual duration of the exposure is collected using the collection field ECCINTD. In some situations, if the actual duration of the interruption is not collected or not derived, this information could be represented in a SUPPEC.QVAL dataset where SUPPEC.QNAM = "ECITRPYN" and SUPPEC.QLABEL = "Exposure Interrupted".

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The collected duration of the study product use interruption.
Variables.Question Text: What was the duration of the interruption in product use?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the duration of the interruption in project use.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPEC dataset as the value of SUPPEC.QVAL where SUPPEC.QNAM="ECITRPD" and SUPPEC.QLABEL= "Interruption Duration". Concatenate the collected interruption duration and the duration unit components and create ECITRPD using ISO 8601 Period format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field is used to collect the duration of the interruption. In some situations, the duration of the interruption may not be collected but calculated from the product start and end times recorded elsewhere in the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit for the collected duration of the interruption in product use.
Variables.Question Text: What was the interruption duration unit?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the unit (e.g., MINUTES, HOURS, DAYS) for the duration of interruption in product use.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPEC dataset as the value of SUPPEC.QVAL where SUPPEC.QNAM = "ECITRPD" and SUPPEC.QLABEL= "Interruption Duration". Concatenate the interruption duration and the duration unit components and create ECITRPD using ISO 8601 Period format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The unit should be collected as a qualifier to the number for duration.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A description of the anatomical location of administration.
Variables.Question Text: What was the anatomical location of the ([study product/dose]) administration?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the body location where the study product was administered (e.g., SHOULDER, HIP, ARM).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collected or preprinted when the applicant needs to identify the specific anatomical location where the study product was administered. LAT, DIR, PORTOT are used to further describe the anatomical location.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier for anatomical location, further detailing side of the body for the study product administration.
Variables.Question Text: What was the side of the anatomical location of the ([study product/dose]) administration?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the side of the body location where the study product was administered (e.g., Left, Right).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Further details the laterality of the location where the study product was administered. This may be preprinted or collected. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier further detailing the position of the anatomical location relative to the center of the body, organ, or specimen.
Variables.Question Text: What was the directionality of the anatomical location of the ([study product/dose]) administration?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the directionality of the body location where the study product was administered (e.g., Anterior, Lower, Proximal, Upper).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be preprinted or collected when the applicant needs to identify the directionality of the anatomical location. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The amount of the prepared product (product + vehicle) used.
Variables.Question Text: What was the total amount (Product + Vehicle) (of [study product/dose]) used?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the total amount (product +vehicle) that was administered/given to the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation variable ECTRTV may also be populated during the process of creating the tabulation datasets.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Administration amount that was used by the subject. \n Note: Should not be the diluent amount alone. The ECTRTV field may be collected if it cannot be determined from other sources.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit of measurement for the prepared product (product + vehicle).
Variables.Question Text: What was the unit for the amount (of [study product/dose] used)?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the unit of total amount (product +vehicle) used by the subject (e.g., mL).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Unit of the used amount

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A text description of the planned timepoint when measurements should be taken, as defined in the protocol.
Variables.Question Text: What was the planned timepoint for [product study /dose] use?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the planned timepoint of study product use if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation time-point anchors ECTPTREF (text description) and ECRFTDTC (date/time) may be needed, as well as tabulation variables ECTPTNUM, ECELTM.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Planned timepoints are needed to differentiate multiple sequential assessments. It is recommended that timepoints should be preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a field that requires the site to enter text. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Planned Time Point" can be included as the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included into the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system-generated. This collection variable is typically collected in all domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Name of the trial epoch with which this element of the arm is associated.
Variables.Question Text: What is the trial epoch?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: [protocol specific]
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: If the same information is collected more than once in different periods/parts of a study (e.g., Disposition), EPOCH may be needed to differentiate them. Typically, the trial epoch will be preprinted on the CRF as the title of the page.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether the subject used study product.
Variables.Question Text: Were any [study product/dose] taken?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the subject used any study products. If Yes, include the appropriate details where indicated.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to a tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The intent/purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring. It provides verification that all other fields on the CRF were deliberately left blank. The EXYN variable is a cleaning or EDC convention meant to indicate that the exposure form should be completed or inserted into the case book.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What is the category of the [study product/dose] ?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the study product category, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, and not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Category" can be included as the column header.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the EXCAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What is the subcategory of the [study product/dose] ?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the study product subcategory, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be preprinted on the CRF or screen and prepopulated in the data management system. This is not typically a question to which the site would provide an answer. EXSCAT can only be used if there is an EXCAT and it must be a subcategorization of EXCAT.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Name of the study product given for the observation.
Variables.Question Text: What was the study product name?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the name of study product.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: EXTRT captures the name of the study product. This is typically collected for open label studies and populated for blinded studies during the tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An internal or external identifier.
Variables.Question Text: What is the [study product/dose] label identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record product label identifier.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This packaging identifier may be collected in different ways.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Lot number of the EXTRT product.
Variables.Question Text: What was the lot number of the [study product/dose] used?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the lot number that appears on the container holding the study product.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The lot number identifies the manufacturing batch of the study product. In open-label studies, the reference number on the study product container may represent an actual lot number and is represented using EXLOT. This variable may be populated during the process of creating the tabulation datasets. Do not collect other identification variables in this field.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dosage form in which the EXTRT is physically presented.
Variables.Question Text: What was the dose form of the [study product/dose]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the dose form or enter the appropriate code from the code list.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This must be collected if it cannot be determined from other sources or if there are multiple options.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The start date of study product, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the ([intended/planned/actual]) ([study product/dose]) (start) date?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the start date of the study product administration using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable EXSTDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Date when the constant interval of the study product use started, or single use occurred. When collecting the date for an individual dose, the word "start" may be omitted from the question text and prompt.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The start time of the study product use, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the ([intended/planned/actual]) ([study product/dose]) (start) time?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the start time (as complete as possible) when administration of study product started.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable EXSTDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Recommend collecting the time a product was started only when a protocol or data collection scenario requires it.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The end date of study product use represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the ([intended/planned/actual]) ([study product/dose]) (end) date?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the end date or last date of administration of study product using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected END DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable EXENDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: If start date and end date are not expected to be on the same date, the end date is required. If the study design indicates that the start and end date are on the same day, the end date is not required because it can be assigned to be equal to the start date.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The end time of study product use, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the ([intended/planned/actual]) ([study product/dose]) (end) time?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the time, (as complete as possible) when study product administration stopped.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected END DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable EXENDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Recommend collecting the time a product was ended when a protocol or data collection scenario requires it. For infusions, the end time of the infusion is typically needed.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Dose (per administration).
Variables.Question Text: What was the dose [per administration] (of [study product/dose]) ?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the dose or amount of study product that was used by the subject in the period recorded; from the start date/time to the end date/time inclusive.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. Numeric values map to tabulation variable EXDOSE. Non-numeric values (e.g., 200-400) map to tabulation variable EXDOSTXT.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Dose or amount taken for single administration of study product or per constant dosing interval recorded. Dose must be collected if it cannot be determined via other methods (e.g., from diary data, product accountability data, protocol). The data collected in this dose text-format field should be mapped to either tabulation variable EXDOSE (if numeric) or EXDOSTXT (if text).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit for intended dose (per administration) for EXDOSE, EXDOSTOT, or EXDOSTXT.
Variables.Question Text: What was the unit for the dose?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the unit of dose or amount taken per period recorded (e.g., ng, mg, mg/kg).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Unit of dose or amount taken per constant dosing interval recorded. Dose unit must be collected if it cannot be determined via other methods (e.g., from protocol). The unit should be preprinted on the CRF or a field provided on the CRF to capture it. A CDASH Subset Controlled Terminology Codelist Name is available for general dose and volume units.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The number of doses given/administered/taken during a specific interval.
Variables.Question Text: What was the frequency of [study product/dose] dosing?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the frequency the study product was administered for a defined period of time.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This may be collected if it cannot be determined from other sources or if there are multiple options. When possible, the options for dose/amount frequency are preprinted on the CRF. When collected, the recommendation is to collect dosing information in separate fields (e.g., ECDOSE, ECDOSEU, ECDOSFRQ) for specific and consistent data collection and to enable programmatically using these data.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The route of administration of the study product.
Variables.Question Text: What was the route of administration (of the [study product/dose] )?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the route of administration (e.g., ORAL) or enter the appropriate code from the code list.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This may be collected if it cannot be determined via other methods (e.g., from protocol) or if there are multiple options.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether the dose was adjusted.
Variables.Question Text: Was the dose adjusted?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Select either Yes or No to indicate whether there was a change in dosing.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: When EXADJ is collected, does not map to a tabulation variable. When EXADJ is not collected, the applicant may represent this variable as a SUPPQ.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Typically, the intent/purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring, as it provides a definitive response regarding any dose changes. It provides verification that the associate field on the CRF (EXADJ) was deliberately left blank. However, the applicant may collect whether the dose was adjusted, without collecting the reason for the change.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Description of or explanation for why a dose of the study product was adjusted.
Variables.Question Text: What was the reason the dose was adjusted (from planned)?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If there was a change in dosing, record the reason for change.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Captures the reason the dose was changed or modified. The reason may be chosen from an applicant-defined list (e.g., adverse event) or entered as free text. May be used for variations from protocol-specified doses or changes from expected doses.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether the exposure was interrupted.
Variables.Question Text: Was the [(study) product/dose] interrupted?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record if there was an interruption in the study product use or dosing.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to a tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The intent/purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring when the actual duration of the exposure is collected using the collection field EXCINTD. In some situations, if the actual duration of the interruption is not collected, or not derived, this information could be represented in a SUPPEX.QVAL dataset where SUPPEX.QNAM = "EXITRPYN" and SUPPEX.QLABEL = "Exposure Interrupted".

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The collected duration of the product interruption.
Variables.Question Text: If the dose was interrupted, how long was the interruption?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the duration of product use interruption.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPEX dataset as the value of SUPPEX.QVAL where SUPPEX.QNAM="EXITRPD" and SUPPEX.QLABEL= "Interruption Duration". Concatenate the collected product interruption duration and the duration unit components and create EXITRPD using ISO 8601 Period format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: In some situations, the duration of the interruption may be calculated from the administration start and end times recorded elsewhere in the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit for the collected duration of product interruption.
Variables.Question Text: If the dose was interrupted, what were the units for the interruption duration?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the unit (e.g., MINUTES, HOURS, DAYS) for the duration of product use interruption.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPEX dataset as the value of SUPPEX.QVAL where SUPPEX.QNAM = "EXITRPD" and SUPPEX.QLABEL= "Interruption Duration". Concatenate the collected interruption duration and the duration unit components and create EXITRPD using ISO 8601 Period format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The unit should be collected and converted into ISO 8601 period format.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A description of the anatomical location of administration.
Variables.Question Text: What was the anatomical location of the ([study product/dose] ) administration?
