Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the body location where the study product was administered (e.g., SHOULDER, HIP, ARM).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collected or preprinted when the applicant needs to identify the specific anatomical location where the study product was administered. LAT, DIR, PORTOT are used to further describe the anatomical location.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The amount of the prepared product (product + vehicle) administered or given.
Variables.Question Text: What was the total amount (product + vehicle)(of [study product/dose] ) administered?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the total amount (product +vehicle) that was administered/given to the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation variable ECTRTV may also be populated during the process of creating the tabulation datasets.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Administration amount that was given to the subject. Note: should not be the diluent amount alone. The ECTRTV field may be collected if it cannot be determined from other sources.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit of measure for the prepared product (product + vehicle).
Variables.Question Text: What was the unit for the amount (of [study product/dose] ) administered?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the unit of total amount (product +vehicle) administered/given to the subject (e.g., mL).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Unit of the administration amount. A CDASH Subset Controlled Terminology Codelist Name is available for dose and volume units.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A text description of the planned timepoint when measurements should be taken, as defined in the protocol.
Variables.Question Text: What was the planned timepoint for [study product/dose] ?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the planned timepoint of study product administration if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation time-point anchors EXTPTREF (text description) and EXRFTDTC (date/time) may be needed, as well as tabulation variables EXTPTNUM, EXELTM.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Planned timepoints are needed to differentiate multiple sequential assessments. It is recommended that timepoints should be preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a field that requires the site to enter text. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Planned Time Point" can be included in the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier for anatomical location, further detailing side of the body for the study product administration.
Variables.Question Text: What was the side of the anatomical location of the ([study product/dose]) administration?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the side of the body location where the study product was administered (e.g., Left, Right).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Further details the laterality of the location where the study product was administered. This may be preprinted or collected. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier further detailing the position of the anatomical location, relative to the center of the body, organ, or specimen.
Variables.Question Text: What was the directionality of the anatomical location of the ([study product/dose]) administration?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the directionality of the body location where the study product was administered (e.g., Anterior, Lower, Proximal, Upper).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be preprinted or collected when the applicant needs to identify the directionality of the anatomical location. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included into the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system generated. This collection variable is typically collected in all collection domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The type of substance (e.g., TOBACCO, ALCOHOL, CAFFEINE or CIGARETTES, CIGARS, COFFEE).
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the [name/type] of (the) substance used?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicants may require different types of substance-use data (e.g., illicit drug use, cigarettes); the value for category may be preprinted on the CRF as a label for the prompt for Substance Use. If a more detailed type of substance appears on the CRF (e.g., CIGARETTES, CIGARS rather than TOBACCO), SUCAT should be TOBACCO and SUTRT should be CIGARETTES.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What is/was the category of the substance (used)?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the Substance Used category, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology (e.g., TOBACCO, ALCOHOL, CAFFEINE). Applicants may require different types of substance-use data (e.g., illicit drug use, cigarettes); the value for category may be preprinted on the CRF. If a more detailed type of substance appears on the CRF (e.g., CIGARETTES, CIGARS, rather than TOBACCO), SUCAT is TOBACCO and SUTRT is CIGARETTES. If the applicant does not specify a type of tobacco on the CRF, SUTRT is TOBACCO. If SUCAT is not collected (e.g., it is evident from the protocol design), it could be populated during the tabulation dataset creation process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the SUCAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the subcategory of the substance (used)?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the Substance Use subcategory, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. The value for subcategory may be preprinted on the CRF or hidden. SUSCAT can only be used if there is a SUCAT and it must be a subcategorization of SUCAT.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication that a specific intervention or a group of interventions is prespecified on a CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: For prespecified interventions, a hidden field on a CRF defaulted to "Y", or added during the tabulation dataset creation. If a study collects both prespecified and free-text interventions, the value of SUPRESP should be "Y" for all prespecified interventions and null for interventions reported as free text.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether any data was collected for the intervention topic.
Variables.Question Text: Were any [applicant-phrase/substance name/recreational drugs] used?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the subject had used any (applicant-defined phrase/recreational drugs/alcohol/substance name).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to a tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: General prompt question to aid in monitoring and data cleaning. This provides verification that all other fields on the CRF were deliberately left blank. This is a field that can be used on any Interventions CRF to indicate whether there is data to record.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Indication the prespecified substance was used.
Variables.Question Text: Has the subject ever [used/consumed] [SUTRT/SUCAT]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Check the appropriate box to indicate if the subject has ever used/consumed tobacco/alcohol/caffeine, currently consumes tobacco/alcohol/caffeine, or formerly used/consumed tobacco/alcohol/caffeine.
Variables.Tabulation Target: SUOCCUR; SUSTRTPT; SUSTRF; SUENRTPT; SUENRF; QVAL
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. May be used to populate SUOCCUR and relative timing variables.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The 3 options (NEVER, CURRENT, FORMER) are applicant-defined in relation to the protocol. If the applicant has specific definitions, these definitions are detailed in the instructions to the site. As this type of response does not correspond exactly to a tabulation variable, collection variable SUNCF is recommended. Applicants must decide how to populate the appropriate relative timing variables when creating the tabulation datasets. For example, If SUNCF ="Never", the value of SUOCCUR will be "N" and all relative timing variables will be null. If the applicant chooses to populate the relative start references (SUSTRTPT, SUSTRF) the value will be "BEFORE" when SUNCF= "CURRENT" and "FORMER". If the applicant also chooses to use relative end references (SUENRF, SUENRTPT), the SUENRTPT value will be "ONGOING" when SUNCF="CURREN" while the value of SUENRF will be "DURING/AFTER". \n Note: When using SUSTRTPT and/or SUENRTPT, these must refer to a time-point anchor (e.g., SCREENING, in SUSTTPT/SUENTPT).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A applicant-defined identifier. This is typically used for preprinted or auto-generated numbers on the CRF, or any other type of identifier that does not already have a defined identifier field.
Variables.Question Text: [Applicant-defined question]
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, applicants may insert instructions to ensure each record has a unique identifier.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. May be used to create RELREC to link this record with a record in another domain.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Because SPID is an applicant-defined identifier, conformance to Question Text or Item Prompt is not applicable. Typically used as an identifier in a data query to communicate clearly to the site the specific record in question or to reconcile data. May be used to record preprinted number (e.g., line number, record number) on the CRF. This field may be populated by the applicant's data collection system.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An explanation for why data are not available.
Variables.Question Text: What was the reason the data was not collected?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Provide the reason why the substance used data were not collected.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The reason data are not available may be chosen from an applicant-defined list (e.g., subject refused) or entered as free text. When PRREASND is used, the tabulation variable PRSTAT should also be populated in the tabulation dataset.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The amount of substance used (e.g., 1-2 packs, 8 oz).
Variables.Question Text: What is/was the amount of [SUTRT] used/consumed?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Check the appropriate box to indicate the amount of tobacco/alcohol/caffeine the subject consumes on a regular basis.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. Numeric values map to SUDOSE in the tabulation dataset. Non-numeric values (e.g., 200-400) map to SUDOSTXT in the tabulation dataset.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Where possible, the options for dose/amount are preprinted on the CRF. In the example given in the definition, "packs" and "ounces" are included as a point of reference. They would be represented as SUDOSU. Care should be taken to map each record to the appropriate tabulation variable SUDOSTXT (text results that cannot be represented in a numeric field) and SUDOSE (numeric results).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The number/amount of the of substance consumed per a specific interval.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the frequency of [SUTRT] [use/consumption]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record how often the subject regularly [uses / consumes] (the) [substance].
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: When possible, the options for dose/amount frequency are preprinted on the CRF. (e.g., PER DAY, PER WEEK, OCCASIONAL).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date substance use started, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY.
Variables.Question Text: What was the start date of [SUTRT/SUCAT] use/consumption?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the start date of the substance use using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable SUSTDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The applicant may choose to capture a complete date or any variation thereof (e.g., month and year, year).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date substance use ended, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the end date of [SUTRT/SUCAT] use/consumption?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the end date of the substance use using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected END DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable SUENDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The applicant may choose to capture a complete date or any variation thereof (e.g., month and year, year).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Collected duration of the substance use.
Variables.Question Text: What was the duration of [SUTRT/SUCAT] use/consumption?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Provide the duration of the substance use (e.g., Record how long the subject has smoked).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenating the collected duration and collected duration unit and populate the tabulation variable SUDUR in ISO 8601 format. Example: P1DT2H (for 1 day, 2 hours).
Variables.Implementation Notes: This is only collected on the CRF if this level of detail is needed and if SUSTDAT and SUENDAT are not collected on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Unit of the collected duration of the substance use. Used only if duration was collected on the CRF.
Variables.Question Text: What was the unit of duration of [SUTRT/SUCAT] use/consumption?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Select the appropriate duration unit of the substance use.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenating the collected duration and collected duration unit and populate the tabulation variable SUDUR in ISO 8601 format. Example: P1DT2H (for 1 day, 2 hours).
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined options should be preprinted on the CRF to avoid making this a free-text field. This will allow the response to be translated into ISO 8601 format.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: If the value for SUTERM is modified for coding purposes, then the modified text is placed here.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This is not a data collection field that would appear on the CRF. If the applicant chooses to code the substance use, the applicant will populate this through the coding process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary or applicant-defined standardized text description of SUTRT, or the modified topic variable (SUMODIFY), if applicable.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This is typically not a data collection field that will appear on the CRF. If the applicant chooses to code the substance use, the applicant will populate this through the coding process. Equivalent to the generic drug name in published (e.g., WHODrug, SNOMED, ICD9) or applicant-defined dictionaries. If SUPRESP is used, and the information about a specific standardized substance name is being solicited, the data from SUTRT may map directly to the tabulation SUDECOD variable.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or the EDC system. This field can be included into the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted for the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system generated. This collection variable is typically collected for all domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM dataset.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether any AEs were experienced during the study.
Variables.Question Text: Were any adverse events experienced?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the subject had any adverse experiences. If Yes, include the appropriate details where indicated on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to an tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The intent/purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring. It provides verification that all other fields on the CRF were deliberately left blank.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What is the category of the adverse experience?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the adverse experience category, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, and not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Category" can be included as the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A subdivision of the AECAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What is the subcategory of the adverse experience?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the adverse experience subcategory, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be preprinted on the CRF or screen and prepopulated in the data management system. This is not typically a question to which the site would provide an answer. AESCAT can only be used if there is an AECAT and it must be a subcategorization of AECAT.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A applicant-defined identifier. This is typically used for preprinted or auto-generated numbers on the CRF, or any other type of identifier that does not already have a defined identifier field.
Variables.Question Text: [Applicant-defined question]
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, applicant may insert instructions to ensure each record has a unique identifier.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. May be used to create RELREC to link this record with a record in another domain.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Because SPID is an applicant-defined identifier, conformance to Question Text or Item Prompt is not applicable. Typically used as an identifier in a data query to communicate clearly to the site the specific record in question or to reconcile concomitant medications, procedures and/or medical history records with AEs. If CMAENO or PRAENO is used, this is the identifier to which CMAENO or PRAENO refers. May be used to record preprinted number (e.g., line number, record number) on the CRF. This field may be populated by the applicant's data collection system.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: Reported Term for the Adverse Experience
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The reported or prespecified name of the adverse experience.
Variables.Question Text: What is the adverse experience term?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record only 1 diagnosis, sign, or symptom per line (e.g., nausea and vomiting should not be recorded in the same entry, but as 2 separate entries). Using accepted medical terminology, enter the diagnosis (if known); otherwise enter a sign or symptom.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Can be represented either as an open-entry field to capture verbatim terms reported by subjects or preprinted, in the situation where solicited AEs of interest are captured. In most cases, the verbatim term (i.e., investigator-reported term) will be coded to a standard medical dictionary (e.g., MedDRA, WHO-ART) after the data have been collected on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether a prespecified adverse experience or a group of adverse experiences occurred when information about the occurrence of a specific experience is solicited.
Variables.Question Text: Did the subject have [prespecified adverse experience/group of adverse experiences]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if [specific adverse experience] has occurred/is occurring, by checking Yes or No.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. The AE domain is intended to hold only adverse experiences that actually happen; all values collected in AEOCCUR for prespecified AEs should be represented in a Findings About Adverse Experiences data set (FAAE) where FAORRES=the value of AEOCCUR where FATESTCD="OCCUR". In addition, where AEOCCUR="Y", there should be a corresponding record in the AE domain.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The collection variable AEOCCUR is used to indicate the occurrence of prespecified adverse experiences (e.g., "Did the subject have high blood pressure?"). AEOCCUR should not be used for spontaneously reported adverse experiences. The site should be able to indicate that the response was not asked or answered.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication that a specific experience or group of experiences are prespecified on a CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A hidden field on a CRF defaulted to "Y", or added during tabulation dataset creation, when the AE is prespecified. Null for spontaneously reported experiences. If a study collects both prespecified and free-text adverse experiences, the value of AEPRESP should be "Y" for all prespecified experiences and null for experiences reported as free text. AEPRESP is a permissible field and may be omitted from the tabulation dataset if all experiences were collected as free text.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The start date of the adverse experience, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What is the adverse experience start date?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the start date of the adverse experience using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable AESTDTC in ISO 8601 format.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The start time of the adverse experience, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What is the adverse experience start time?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the start time (as complete as possible) of the adverse experience.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable AESTDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collecting the time an AE started is only appropriate if it can be realistically determined and if there is a scientific reason for needing to know this level of detail.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A description of the anatomical location relevant for the adverse experience.
Variables.Question Text: What is the anatomical location of the adverse experience?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate the anatomical location of the adverse experience.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collected or preprinted when the applicant needs to identify the specific anatomical location. applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF. LAT, DIR, PORTOT are used to further describe the anatomical location.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier for anatomical location, further detailing the side of the body relevant for the experience.
Variables.Question Text: What is the side of the anatomical location of the adverse experience?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the side of the anatomical location of the adverse experience.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be preprinted or collected when the applicant needs to identify the specific side of the anatomical location. applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier further detailing the position of the anatomical location, relative to the center of the body, organ, or specimen.
Variables.Question Text: What is the directionality of the anatomical location of the adverse experience?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the directionality of the anatomical location of the adverse experience.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be preprinted or collected when the applicant needs to identify the directionality of the anatomical location. applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier for anatomical location, further detailing the distribution (i.e., arrangement of, apportioning of).
Variables.Question Text: What is the portion or totality of the anatomical location of the adverse experience?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate the portion or totality anatomical location of the adverse experience.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collected when the applicant needs to identify the specific portionality for the anatomical locations. applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Indication that an adverse experience is ongoing when no end date is provided.
Variables.Question Text: Is the adverse experience ongoing (as of [the study-specific time point or period])?
Variables.Prompt: Ongoing (as of [the study-specific time point or period])
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the adverse experience has not resolved at the time of data collection; leave the End Date blank.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. May be used to populate a value into a tabulation relative timing variable such as AEENRF or AEENRTPT. When populating AEENRF, if the value of AEONGO is "Y", the value of "DURING", "AFTER" or "DURING/AFTER" may be used. When populating AEENRTPT, if the value of AEONGO is "Y", the value of "ONGOING" may be used. When AEONGO refers to the Reference Period (defined in DM.RFSTDTC to DM.RFENDTC) the tabulation variable AEENRF should be populated. When AEONGO is compared to another time point, the tabulation variables AEENRTPT and AEENTPT should be used. Note: AEENRTPT must refer to a time-point anchor described in AEENTPT.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Completed to indicate that the AE has not resolved at the time of data collection, when no end date is collected. In some cases the ongoing status may be determined from AE Outcome. The purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring; this field provides further confirmation that End Date was deliberately left blank. Often used as a tick/checkbox.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date when the adverse experience resolved/ended, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the adverse experience end date?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the date that the adverse experience. resolved using this format (DD-MON-YYYY). If the AE is ongoing, leave the field blank.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected END DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable AEENDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The definition of resolved is applicant-specific. The preferred method is to collect a complete end date (if applicable). Partial dates (e.g., providing year only, month and year only) may be acceptable.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The time when the adverse experience ended/resolved, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the adverse experience end time?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the time (as complete as possible) that the adverse experience resolved.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected END DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable AEENDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collecting the time an AE resolved is only appropriate if it can be realistically determined and if there is a scientific reason for needing to know this level of detail.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The severity or intensity of the experience.
Variables.Question Text: What is the severity of the adverse experience?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: The reporting physician/healthcare professional will assess the severity of the experience using the applicant-defined categories. This assessment is subjective and the reporting physician/ healthcare professional should use medical judgment to compare the reported adverse experience to similar type experiences observed in clinical practice. Severity is not equivalent to seriousness.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Either AESEV or AETOXGR must appear on the CRF. Some studies may mandate the collection of both.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The grade of the severity of the experience using a standard "toxicity" scale (e.g., NCI CTCAE).
Variables.Question Text: What is the [NCI CTCAE/Name of scale (toxicity) grade] of the adverse experience?
Variables.Prompt: [NCI CTCAE/ Name of the scale] (Toxicity) Grade
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: The reporting physician/healthcare professional will assess the severity of the adverse experience using the specified grades scale.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The applicant is expected to provide the toxicity scale name and version used to map the terms utilizing the Define-XML external codelist attributes.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Either AESEV or AETOXGR must appear on the CRF. Some studies may mandate the collection of both. Published toxicity-like scales can be used.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether the adverse experience is determined to be "serious," based on what is defined in the protocol.
Variables.Question Text: Was the adverse experience serious?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Assess if the adverse experience should be classified as "serious," based on the criteria defined in the protocol.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field is related to the individual SAE-type fields, which may or may not be collected on the CRF. Either AESER or all the SAE-type fields must be present on the CRF. Applicants should consult with regulatory agencies regarding the collection of this data.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication the serious adverse experience resulted in death.
Variables.Question Text: Did the adverse experience result in death?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether the serious adverse experience resulted in death.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: If details regarding SAEs are collected in the clinical database, then it is recommended that a separate Yes/No variable be defined for each SAE type. applicants may only collect the AESER field when collecting individual SAE types in a separate database. Applicants should consult with regulatory agencies regarding the collection of this data.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Date of death for any subject who died.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the subject's date of death?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the date of death.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field does not map directly to an tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable DTHDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: In the CDASH model, Death Date is a timing variable; it is not included as a timing variable in the SDTM. It may be collected on any CRF deemed appropriate by the applicant, but should only be collected once. The tabulation variable DTHDTC is mapped to the DM domain during the tabulation dataset creation process. The tabulation variable DM.DTHFLG is not a collection variable, but it is typically populated during the tabulation dataset creation process. Death Date may be mapped to other tabulation domains, as deemed appropriate by the applicant (e.g., DS).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication the serious adverse experience was life threatening.
Variables.Question Text: Was the adverse experience life threatening?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether the serious adverse experience is life threatening.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: If details regarding SAEs are collected in the clinical database, then it is recommended that a separate Yes/No variable be defined for each SAE type. applicants may only collect the AESER field when collecting individual SAE types in a separate pharmacovigilance database. applicants should consult with regulatory agencies regarding the collection of this data.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication the serious adverse experience resulted in an initial or prolonged hospitalization.
Variables.Question Text: Did the adverse experience result in initial or prolonged hospitalization for the subject?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether the serious adverse experience resulted in an initial or prolonged hospitalization.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: If details regarding SAEs are collected in the clinical database, then it is recommended that a separate Yes/No variable be defined for each SAE type. applicants may only collect the AESER field when collecting individual SAE types in a separate pharmacovigilance database. applicants should consult with regulatory agencies regarding the collection of this data.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication the serious adverse experience was associated with a persistent or significant disability or incapacity.
Variables.Question Text: Did the adverse experience result in disability or permanent damage?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether the serious adverse experience resulted in a persistent or significant disability or incapacity.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: If details regarding SAEs are collected in the clinical database, then it is recommended that a separate Yes/No variable be defined for each SAE type. applicants may only collect the AESER field when collecting individual SAE types in a separate pharmacovigilance database. applicants should consult with regulatory agencies regarding the collection of this data.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication the serious adverse experience was associated with a congenital anomaly or birth defect.
Variables.Question Text: Was the adverse experience associated with a congenital anomaly or birth defect?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether the serious adverse experience was associated with congenital anomaly or birth defect.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: If details regarding SAEs are collected in the clinical database, then it is recommended that a separate Yes/No variable be defined for each SAE type. Applicants may only collect the AESER field when collecting individual SAE types in a separate pharmacovigilance database. applicants should consult with regulatory agencies regarding the collection of this data.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication an adverse experience required medical or surgical intervention to preclude permanent impairment of a body function, or prevent permanent damage to a body structure, due to the use of a medical product.
Variables.Question Text: Did the adverse experience require intervention to prevent permanent impairment or damage resulting from the use of a medical product?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether the serious adverse experience required intervention to prevent permanent impairment or damage due to the use of a medical product.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. applicants should refer to requirements for reporting adverse experiences involving medical devices.
Variables.Implementation Notes: If details regarding SAEs are collected in the clinical database, then it is recommended that a separate Yes/No variable be defined for each SAE type. Applicants may only collect the AESER field when collecting individual SAE types in a separate database. Applicants should consult with regulatory agencies regarding the collection of this data.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication additional categories for seriousness apply.
Variables.Question Text: Was the adverse experience a medically important event not covered by other serious criteria?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether the serious adverse experience is an "important medical exvent," which may be defined in the protocol or in the investigator brochure.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: If details regarding SAEs are collected in the clinical database, then it is recommended that a separate Yes/No variable be defined for each SAE type. Applicants may only collect the AESER field when collecting individual SAE types in a separate database. Applicants should consult with regulatory agencies regarding the collection of this data.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication the serious experience was associated with the development of cancer.
Variables.Question Text: Was the adverse experience associated with the development of cancer?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether the serious adverse experience was associated with development of cancer.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: If details regarding SAEs are collected in the clinical database, then it is recommended that a separate Yes/No variable be defined for each SAE type. Applicants may only collect the AESER field when collecting individual SAE types in a separate database. Applicants should consult with regulatory agencies regarding the collection of this data.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication the serious experience occurred with an overdose.
Variables.Question Text: Did the adverse experience occur with an overdose?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether the serious adverse experience occurred with an overdose.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: If details regarding SAEs are collected in the clinical database, then it is recommended that a separate Yes/No variable be defined for each SAE type. Applicants may only collect the AESER field when collecting individual SAE types in a separate pharmacovigilance database. Applicants should consult with regulatory agencies regarding the collection of this data.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication the study product had a causal effect on the adverse experience, as determined by the clinician/investigator.
Variables.Question Text: Was this adverse experience related to study product?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the cause of the adverse experience is related to the study product and cannot be reasonably explained by other factors (e.g., subject's clinical state, concomitant therapy, other interventions).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology is used to indicate the relationship between the AE and the study product. It is recommended that applicants check with the regulatory authority for population of this variable to ensure it meets expectations for submission. There is no industry-wide controlled terminology for relationship to product exposure. It is recommended that applicants establish terminology and apply it consistently.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A description of the action taken with study product as a result of the experience.
Variables.Question Text: What action was taken with study product?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record changes made to the study product resulting from the adverse experience.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: CDISC Controlled Terminology is used to indicate the action taken with the product in response to the AE. How to handle multiple actions taken is up to the applicant. If this information is collected elsewhere (e.g., on the Exposure CRF), then it is not required to be collected on the AE CRF. This variable is not to be used for actions taken with devices.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A description of the action taken, with respect to a device used in a study (which may or may not be the device under study), as a result of the experience.
Variables.Question Text: What action was taken with a device used in the study?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record actions taken resulting from the adverse experience that are related to a study or non-study device.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly an tabulation variable. Applicants may represent this data in a SUPPAE dataset where SUPPAE.QNAM = "AEACNDEV" and SUPPAE.QLABEL = "Actions Taken with Device".
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology for actions that are related to the device.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A description of other action taken as a result of the experience that is unrelated to dose adjustments of the study product.
Variables.Question Text: What other action was taken?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record all other action(s) taken resulting from the adverse experience that are unrelated to study products given because of this AE.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This is usually collected as a free-text field. If possible/desired, the applicant can create controlled terminology.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A description of the outcome of an experience.
Variables.Question Text: What is the outcome of this adverse experience?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the appropriate outcome of the experience in relation to the subject's status.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: CDISC Controlled Terminology is used to indicate the outcome of the experience as it relates to the subject's status. The use of this field is the recommended way to describe whether and how the AE resolved. Because the outcome of an AE may be death, if this field is not used, be sure to provide another form (e.g., Disposition) with clear instructions to record deaths there.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether the experience caused the subject to discontinue from the study.
Variables.Question Text: Did the adverse experience cause the subject to be discontinued from the study?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record if the adverse experience caused the subject to discontinue from the study.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly an tabulation variable. May be used to create a RELREC tabulation dataset to link the AE to the DS dataset record. Applicants may also represent this data in a SUPPAE dataset where SUPPAE.QNAM = "AEDIS" and SUPPAE.QLABEL = "Caused Study Discontinuation", if appropriate.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Because the Action Taken field only collects changes made in relation to the study product due to the AE, an additional field was created to identify the AE(s) that caused the subject to discontinue from the study. Some applicants opt to capture this information only on the Subject Disposition CRF. Others choose to collect this data on both the DS and AE CRFs so that specific AE term(s) and related data can be identified. If the CRF is designed to link the DS and AE tabulation records, then RELREC can be used to identify that relationship.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: AE Relationship to Non-Study Trtmnt or Prod
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication whether, in the investigator's opinion, the experience may have been due to a product other than study product.
Variables.Question Text: Was this adverse experience due to product other than study product?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if this adverse experience was due to product other than study product. If Yes, briefly describe this non-study product relationship.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to a tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The intent/purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring. It provides verification that the AERELNST collection field on the CRF was deliberately left blank.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: AE Relationship to Non-Study Trtmnt or Prod
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Description of the investigator's opinion as to whether the adverse experience may have been due to a product other than study product.
Variables.Question Text: What is the relationship to non-study product?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the investigator's opinion as to whether the experience may have been due to a product other than study product.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be reported as free text (e.g., "MORE LIKELY RELATED TO ASPIRIN USE"). If possible/desired, applicants can create controlled terminology.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An adverse experience of special interest (serious or non-serious) is one of scientific and medical concern specific to the applicant's product or program, for which ongoing monitoring and rapid communication by the investigator to the applicant can be appropriate. Such an experience might warrant further investigation in order to characterize and understand it. Depending on the nature of the experience, rapid communication by the study applicant to other parties (e.g., regulators) might also be warranted.
Variables.Question Text: Is this experience of special interest?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the investigator's opinion as to whether the experience is an adverse experience of special interest by the applicant.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to a tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This collection field may be used just to trigger other CRF pages, or populate a value in AECAT or AESCAT. This information could be represented in a SUPPAE dataset where SUPPAE.QNAM = "AESI" and SUPPAE.QLABEL = "Adverse experience of Special Interest.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Used to indicate the pattern of the experience over time.
Variables.Question Text: What is the adverse experience pattern?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: For each adverse experience, check the pattern of the AE. If a single experience, choose Single.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Used to report the pattern of the AE (e.g., "INTERMITTENT", "CONTINUOUS", "SINGLE EVENT"). For crossover studies, it is not recommended to capture this field for intermittent AEs. Instead, the AE should have corresponding start and stop dates to capture when the AE started and stopped.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication whether a concomitant or additional product given because of the occurrence of the experience.
Variables.Question Text: Was a concomitant or additional product given due to this adverse experience?
Variables.Prompt: Concomitant or Additional Product Given Due to This AE
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if any non-study treatments or products were received because of this adverse experience. If Yes, medications should be recorded on the ConMed CRF and procedures recorded on the Procedures CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: If medication data are reported, the CMAENO variable (on the CM CRF) may be used to collect the associated AE Identifier in order to populate RELREC. If procedures are reported, the PRAENO variable (on the PR CRF) may be used to collect the associated AE Identifier in order to populate RELREC.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: If the value for AETERM is modified to facilitate coding, then AEMODIFY will contain the modified text.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This is not a data collection field that would appear on the CRF. applicants will populate this through the coding process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary or standardized text description of AETERM or the modified topic variable (AEMODIFY), if applicable.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. Applicants should provide the dictionary name and version used to map terms utilizing Define-XML external codelist attributes.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This is typically not a data collection field that would appear on the CRF. applicants will populate this through the coding process. Equivalent to the Preferred Term (PT) in MedDRA.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived text description of the lowest level term.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. Applicants should provide the dictionary name and version used to map terms utilizing Define-XML external codelist attributes. Applicants should include an Origin in the define metadata document to indicate that the data was "ASSIGNED".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived code for the lowest level term.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. Applicants should provide the dictionary name and version used to map terms utilizing Define-XML external codelist attributes. Applicants should include an Origin in the define metadata document to indicate that the data was "ASSIGNED".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived code for the preferred term.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. Applicants should provide the dictionary name and version used to map terms utilizing Define-XML external codelist attributes. Applicants should include an Origin in the define metadata document to indicate that the data was "ASSIGNED".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived text description of the high level term for the primary system organ class (SOC).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. Applicants should provide the dictionary name and version used to map terms utilizing Define-XML external codelist attributes. Applicants should include an Origin in the define metadata document to indicate that the data was "ASSIGNED".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived code for the high level term for the primary SOC.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. Applicants should provide the dictionary name and version used to map terms utilizing Define-XML external codelist attributes. Applicants should include an Origin in the define metadata document to indicate that the data was "ASSIGNED".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived text description of the high level group term for the primary SOC.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. Applicants should provide the dictionary name and version used to map terms utilizing Define-XML external codelist attributes. Applicants should include an Origin in the define metadata document to indicate that the data was "ASSIGNED".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: AE High Level Group Term Code
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived code for the high level group term for the primary SOC.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. Applicants should provide the dictionary name and version used to map terms utilizing Define-XML external codelist attributes. Applicants should include an Origin in the define metadata document to indicate that the data was "ASSIGNED".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived text description of the primary SOC.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. Applicants should provide the dictionary name and version used to map terms utilizing Define-XML external codelist attributes. Applicants should include an Origin in the define metadata document to indicate that the data was "ASSIGNED".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding. Will be the same as the AEBODSYS if the primary SOC was used for analysis.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: AE Primary System Organ Class Code
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived code for the primary SOC.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. Applicants should provide the dictionary name and version used to map terms utilizing Define-XML external codelist attributes. Applicants should include an Origin in the define metadata document to indicate that the data was "ASSIGNED".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. Applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding. Will be the same as AEBDSYCD if the primary SOC was used for analysis.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication whether any other actions were taken in response to the adverse experience that were unrelated to study product changes or other treatments/products given because of this adverse experience.
Variables.Question Text: Were any other actions taken in response to this adverse experience?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate whether any other action(s) were taken in response to the adverse experience that are unrelated to study product changes or other treatments/products given because of this experience. If Yes, briefly describe these actions.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to a tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The intent/purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring. It provides verification that the AEACNOTH field on the CRF was deliberately left blank.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included in the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system-generated. This collection variable is typically collected in all collection domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What is the category of the protocol deviation?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the deviation category, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Category" can be included as the column header.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the DVCAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What is the subcategory of the protocol deviation?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the deviation event subcategory, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be preprinted on the CRF or screen and prepopulated in the data management system. This is not typically a question to which the site would provide an answer. DVSCAT can only be used if there is an DVCAT, and it must be a subcategorization of DVCAT.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether there were any protocol deviations.
Variables.Question Text: Were there any protocol deviations?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Enter Yes if a protocol deviation occurred and No if none occurred. Ensure that any adverse event which triggers a protocol deviation (e.g., concomitant medication use, newly discovered medical history) is noted in the respective CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to a tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The intent/purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring. It provides verification that all other fields on the CRF were deliberately left blank.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The applicant-defined standardized text for the name of the protocol deviation.
Variables.Question Text: What was the (standardized) protocol deviation (term/(code)?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record protocol deviations identified and/or select the appropriate code from the list of protocol deviation terms.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: DVTERM and DVDECOD may have the same value. If the CRF is collecting protocol deviations using a codelist of responses, then DVDECOD should be used to store the codelist response. Appicants must use either DVDECOD or DVTERM on the CRF and, in some cases, both may be used. For example, if the CRF collects "Specify, Other" or similar additional free-text descriptions of codelist items, then DVTERM should be used to store the detailed descriptive text.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The reported or prespecified name of the protocol deviation.
Variables.Question Text: What was the protocol deviation term?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the appropriate code from the list of protocol deviation terms.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: DVTERM and DVDECOD may have the same value. If the CRF is collecting protocol deviations using a free-text field, then DVTERM should be used to store the free-text response. Applicants may use either DVDECOD or DVTERM on the CRF, but a value in DVTERM is required in the tabulation datasets.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The start date of deviation, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the protocol deviation start date?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the start date that the protocol deviation using this format (DD-MON-YYYY). This should be the start or occurrence of the protocol deviation, not the date it was discovered or reported.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable DVSTDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This may be derived if not collected on a CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The start time of the deviation, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the protocol deviation start time?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If appropriate, record the start time (as complete as possible) of the protocol deviation in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss). This should be the start or occurrence of the protocol deviation, not the time it was discovered or reported.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable DVSTDTC in ISO 8601 format.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The end date of the deviation, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the protocol deviation end date?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the end date of the protocol deviation using this format (DD-MON-YYYY). This should be the date the protocol deviation stopped, not the date it was discovered or reported.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected END DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable DVENDTC in ISO 8601 format.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The end time of the deviation, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the protocol deviation end time?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If appropriate, record the end time (as complete as possible) of the protocol deviation in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss). This should be the time the protocol deviation stopped, not the time it was discovered or reported.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected END DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable DVENDTC in ISO 8601 format.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An applicant-defined identifier. This is typically used for preprinted or auto-generated numbers on the CRF, or any other type of identifier that does not already have a defined identifier field.
Variables.Question Text: [Applicant-defined question]
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, the applicant may insert instructions to ensure each record has a unique identifier.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. May be used to create RELREC to link this record with a record in another domain.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Because SPID is an applicant-defined identifier, conformance to Question Text or Item Prompt is not applicable. Typically used as an identifier in a data query to communicate clearly to the site the specific record in question or to reconcile data. May be used to record preprinted number (e.g., line number, record number) on the CRF. This field may be populated by the applicant's data collection system.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or the EDC system. This field can be included into the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted for the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system generated. This collection variable is typically collected for all domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM dataset. R/C rather than HR because events may happen to or with a device that do not involved subjects, and may even be before the device was in contact with a subject.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Applicant-Defined Tobacco Product ID
Variables.Question Text: [Applicant-defined question]
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the study device.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Identifier used to uniquely identify a tobacco product across all studies for all applications/submissions involving the product.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether any tobacco device events were experienced during the study.
Variables.Question Text: Were any tobacco device events experienced?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the subject experienced any tobacco device events. If Yes, include the appropriate details where indicated on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to an tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The intent/purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring. It provides verification that all other fields on the CRF were deliberately left blank.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What is the category of the device Event?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the device event category, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, and not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Category" can be included as the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the EMCAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What is the subcategory of the device event?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the device event subcategory, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be preprinted on the CRF or screen and prepopulated in the data management system. This is not typically a question to which the site would provide an answer. EMSCAT can only be used if there is an EMCAT and it must be a subcategorization of EMCAT.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An applicant-defined identifier. This is typically used for preprinted or auto-generated numbers on the CRF, or any other type of identifier that does not already have a defined identifier field.
Variables.Question Text: [Applicant-defined question]
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, applicant may insert instructions to ensure each record has a unique identifier.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. May be used to create RELREC to link this record with a record in another domain.
