Variables.Implementation Notes: Because SPID is an applicant-defined identifier, conformance to Question Text or Item Prompt is not applicable. Typically used as an identifier in a data query to communicate clearly to the site the specific record in question or to reconcile concomitant medications, procedures and/or medical history records with AEs or device events. If CMAENO or PRAENO is used, this is the identifier to which CMAENO or PRAENO refers. May be used to record preprinted number (e.g., line number, record number) on the CRF. This field may be populated by the applicant's data collection system.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: Reported Term for the Device Event
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The reported or prespecified name of the device event.
Variables.Question Text: What is the device event term?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record only 1 device event. Use accepted terminology.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Can be represented either as an open-entry field to capture verbatim terms reported by subjects or preprinted, in the situation where solicited device events of interest are captured. In most cases, the verbatim term (i.e. investigator-reported term) will be coded to a a standard dictionary.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether a prespecified device event or a group of device events occurred when information about the occurrence of a specific event is solicited.
Variables.Question Text: Did the subject have [prespecified device event/group of device events]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if [specific Device Event] has occurred/is occurring, by checking Yes or No.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The collection variable EMOCCUR is used to indicate the occurrence of prespecified device events (e.g. "Did the the device batteries malfunction? \n EMOCCUR should not be used for spontaneously reported device events. The site should be able to indicate that the response was not asked or answered.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication that a specific event or group of events are prespecified on a CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A hidden field on a CRF defaulted to "Y", or added during tabulation dataset creation, when the EMis prespecified. Null for spontaneously reported events. If a study collects both prespecified and free-text device events, the value of EMPRESP should be "Y" for all prespecified events and null for events reported as free-text. EMPRESP is a permissible field. and may be omitted from the tabulation dataset if all events were collected as free text.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The start date of the device event, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What is the device event start date?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the start date of the device event using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable EMSTDTC in ISO 8601 format.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The start time of the device event, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What is the device event start time?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the start time (as complete as possible) of the device event.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable EMSTDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collecting the time an event resolved is only appropriate if it can be realistically determined and if there is a scientific reason for needing to know this level of detail.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Indication that an device event is ongoing when no end date is provided.
Variables.Question Text: Is the device event ongoing (as of [the study-specific time point or period])?
Variables.Prompt: Ongoing (as of [the study-specific time point or period])
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the device event has not resolved at the time of data collection; leave the End Date blank.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. May be used to populate a value into a tabulation relative timing variable such as EMENRF or EMENRTPT. When populating EMENRF, if the value of EMONGO is "Y", the value of "DURING", "AFTER" or "DURING/AFTER" may be used. When populating EMENRTPT, if the value of EMONGO is "Y", the value of "ONGOING" may be used. When EMONGO refers to the Reference Period (defined in DM.RFSTDTC to DM.RFENDTC) the tabulation variable EMENRF should be populated. When EMONGO is compared to another time point, the tabulation variables EMENRTPT and EMENTPT should be used. Note: EMENRTPT must refer to a timepoint anchor described in EMENTPT.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Completed to indicate that the event has not resolved at the time of data collection, when no end date is collected. In some cases the ongoing status may be determined from Outcome. The purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring; this field provides further confirmation that End Date was deliberately left blank. Often used as a tick/checkbox.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date when the device event resolved/ended, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the device event end date?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the date that the device event. resolved using this format (DD-MON-YYYY). If the EMis ongoing, leave the field blank.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected END DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable EMENDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The definition of resolved is applicant-specific. The preferred method is to collect a complete end date (if applicable). Partial dates (e.g., providing year only, month and year only) may be acceptable.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The time when the Device Event ended/resolved, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the Device Event end time?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the time (as complete as possible) that the Device Event resolved.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected END DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable EMENDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collecting the time an event resolved is only appropriate if it can be realistically determined and if there is a scientific reason for needing to know this level of detail.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The severity or intensity of the event.
Variables.Question Text: What is the severity of the device event?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: The reporting physician/healthcare professional will assess the severity of the event using the applicant-defined categories. This assessment is subjective and the reporting physician/ healthcare professional should use judgment to compare the reported device event to similar type events observed. Severity is not equivalent to seriousness.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A description of the action taken, with respect to a device used in a study (which may or may not be the device under study), as a result of the event.
Variables.Question Text: What action was taken with a device used in the study?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record actions taken resulting from the device event that are related to a study or non-study device.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology for actions that are related to the device (e.g., device replacement, battery replacement.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An device event of special interest (serious or non-serious) is one of scientific and medical concern specific to the applicant's product or program, for which ongoing monitoring and rapid communication by the investigator to the applicant can be appropriate. Such an event might warrant further investigation in order to characterize and understand it. Depending on the nature of the event, rapid communication by the study applicant to other parties (e.g., regulators) might also be warranted.
Variables.Question Text: Is this event of special interest?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the investigator's opinion as to whether the event is an device event of special interest by the applicant.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to a tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This collection field may be used just to trigger other CRF pages, or populate a value in EMCAT or EMSCAT. This information could be represented in a SUPPEM dataset where SUPPEM.QNAM = "EMSI" and SUPPEM.QLABEL = "Device Event of Special Interest.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Used to indicate the pattern of the event over time.
Variables.Question Text: What is the device event pattern?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: For each device event, check the pattern of the device event, If a single event, choose Single.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Used to report the pattern of the EM (e.g.,"INTERMITTENT", "CONTINUOUS", "SINGLE EVENT"). For crossover studies, it is not recommended to capture this field for intermittent events. Instead, the corresponding start and stop dates should be captured.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: If the value for EMTERM is modified to facilitate coding, then EMMODIFY will contain the modified text.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This is not a data collection field that would appear on the CRF. applicants will populate this through the coding process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary or standardized text description of EMTERM or the modified topic variable (EMMODIFY), if applicable.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The applicant is expected to provide the dictionary name and version used to map the terms utilizing the Define-XML external codelist attributes.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This is typically not a data collection field that would appear on the CRF. applicants will populate this through the coding process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included into the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system-generated. This collection variable is typically collected in all domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether there was any medical history to report.
Variables.Question Text: Were any medical conditions or events reported?; Has the subject had any medical conditions or events?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the subject experienced any medical conditions or events. If Yes, include the appropriate details where indicated on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to a tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The intent/purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring. It provides verification that all other fields on the CRF were deliberately left blank.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the category of the medical history?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, the applicant provides instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology (e.g., CARDIAC, GENERAL). This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Category" can be included as the column header. This would be used when specific medical history is captured, in addition to the general medical history.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the MHCAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the subcategory of the medical history?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, the applicant provides instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be preprinted on the CRF or screen and prepopulated in the data management system. This is not typically a question to which the site would provide an answer. Typically would be used when specific medical history (e.g., disease diagnosis) is captured, in addition to the general medical history. MHSCAT can only be used if there is an MHCAT, and it must be a subcategorization of MHCAT.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date on which the medical history was collected, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the date the medical history was collected?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the date on which the medical history was collected using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable MHDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This should be a complete date. The date of collection may be determined from a collected visit date.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A applicant-defined identifier. This is typically used for preprinted or auto-generated numbers on the CRF, or any other type of identifier that does not already have a defined identifier field.
Variables.Question Text: [Applicant-defined question]
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, applicant may insert instructions to ensure each record has a unique identifier.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. May be used to create RELREC to link this record with a record in another domain.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Because SPID is a applicant-defined identifier, conformance to Question Text or Item Prompt is not applicable. Typically used as an identifier in a data query to communicate clearly to the site the specific record in question or to reconcile concomitant medications and/or procedure records with MH. May be used to record preprinted number (e.g. line number, record number) on the CRF. This field may be populated by the applicant's data collection system. If CMMHNO or PRMHNO is used, this is the identifier to which CMMHNO or PRMHNO refers.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Specifies the aspect of the medical condition or event by which MHSTDTC and/or MHENDTC is defined.
Variables.Question Text: What was the medical history event date type?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: The instructions depend upon the format of the CRF. Applicants may print these values on the CRF or use them as defaulted or hidden text.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The type of start/ and or end date (e.g.,, DIAGNOSIS, SYMPTOMS, RELAPSE, INFECTION). It is not related to the trial's condition. This date type cannot be a PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS, SECONDARY DIAGNOSIS because these terms do not define the date type.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: Reported Term for the Medical History
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The reported or prespecified name of the medical condition or event.
Variables.Question Text: What is the medical condition or event term?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record all relevant medical conditions or events, as defined in the protocol. Record only 1 medical condition or event per line. Ensure that the medical conditions or events listed on the Medical History page do not meet any of the exclusion criteria.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicants should collect all relevant medical conditions or events, as defined in the protocol. It is a best practice for Applicants to collect all relevant history of surgeries or procedures using the associated diagnosis in the MH domain, while reporting relevant surgeries and procedures in the tabulation PR domain. Applicants should provide instructions on how surgeries and procedures will be handled based on the protocol requirements. Information on specified surgeries or procedures should be collected in the PR domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether a prespecified medical condition/event or a group of medical conditions/events occurred when information about the occurrence of a specific event is solicited.
Variables.Question Text: Did the subject have [prespecified medical condition/event/group of medical conditions]; Is the [prespecified medical occurring]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if [specific medical condition/event] has occurred/is occurring by checking Yes or No.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: MHOCCUR is used to report the occurrence of specified medical conditions or events. MHOCCUR is not used if the medical conditions or events are collected on the CRF in a manner that requires spontaneously free-text response. The site should be able to indicate that the question was not asked or answered.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication that a specific event, or group of events, are prespecified on a CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A hidden field on a CRF defaulted to "Y", or added during the tabulation dataset creation when the medical condition or event is prespecified. Null for spontaneously reported events. If a study collects both prespecified medical history and free-text events, the value of MHPRESP should be "Y" for all prespecified events and null for medical conditions or events reported as free text. MHPRESP is a permissible and may be omitted from the tabulation dataset if all events were collected as free text.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether the event occurred prior to study start.
Variables.Question Text: Did the medical condition or event start prior to [MHSTTPT]?; Did the medical condition or event start prior to study start?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Check if the medical condition or event started [before the study].
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. May be used to populate a value into a tabulation relative timing variable such as MHSTRF or MHSTRTPT. When populating MHSTRF, or MHSTRTPT, if the value of the collection field MHPRIOR is "Y" a value from the CDISC CT (STENRF) may be used. When MHPRIOR refers to the Study Reference Period (defined in DM.RFSTDTC to DM.RFENDTC) the tabulation variable MHSTRF should be populated. When MHPRIOR is compared to another time point, the tabulation variables MHSTRTPT and MHSTTPT should be used. Note: MHSTRTPT must refer to the timepoint anchor described in MHSTTPT.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicants may collect this information rather than start dates.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Indication the medical condition or event is ongoing when no end date is provided.
Variables.Question Text: Is the medical condition or event ongoing (as of the [study-specific timepoint or period])?
Variables.Prompt: Ongoing (as of the [study-specific timepoint or period])
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the medical condition or event as ongoing ("Y") if it has not ended at the time of data collection. If the medical condition or event is ongoing, the end date should be left blank.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. May be used to populate a value into a tabulation relative timing variable such as MHENRF or MHENRTPT. When populating MHENRF, if the value of MHONGO is "Y", the value of "DURING", "AFTER" or "DURING/AFTER" may be used. When populating MHENRTPT, if the value of MHONGO is "Y", the value of "ONGOING" may be used. When MHONGO refers to the Study Reference Period (defined in DM.RFSTDTC to DM.RFENDTC) the tabulation variable MHENRF should be populated. When MHONGO is compared to another time point, the tabulation variables MHENRTPT and MHENTPT should be used. \n Note: MHENRTPT must refer to a timepoint anchor described in MHENTPT.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Completed to indicate that the condition has not resolved at the time of data collection. It is expected that every reported condition has either an end date or the Ongoing field is populated, but not both.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: MH Disease or Symptom Under Control
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Indication of whether the medical condition or event is under control at the time of data collection.
Variables.Question Text: Is the medical condition or event under control?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Select the most appropriate response.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPMH dataset as the value of SUPPMH.QVAL where SUPPMH.QNAM ="MHCTRL" and SUPPMH.LABEL="Medical Condition Under Control".
Variables.Implementation Notes: MHCTRL is not defined in the tabulation MH domain. If collected, it should be represented in the SUPPMH dataset. If MHCTRL is collected, the applicant must provide information on the relative timeframe. Generally, MHDAT is collected or determined using the visit date of the collection to indicate this is the subject's status at the time of data collection.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The start date of medical history event or condition, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the [medical event or condition/category of the event] start date?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the start date of the medical event or condition using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable MHSTDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The applicant may choose to capture a complete date or any variation thereof (e.g., month and year, year).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The end date of medical history event or condition, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What[is/was] the[medical event or condition/category of the event] end date?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the end date of the medical event or condition using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected END DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable MHENDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The applicant may choose to capture a complete date or any variation thereof (e.g., month and year, year).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A description of the anatomical location relevant for the medical condition or event.
Variables.Question Text: What was the anatomical location of the medical condition or event?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate the anatomical location of the medical event or condition.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collected or preprinted when the applicant needs to identify the specific anatomical location (e.g., ARM for skin rash). Could be a defaulted or hidden field on the CRF for prespecified [MHTERM/Event Topic]. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF. LAT, DIR, PORTOT are used to further describe the anatomical location.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier for anatomical location, further detailing the side of the body relevant for the event.
Variables.Question Text: What was the side of the anatomical location of the medical condition or event?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the side of the anatomical location of the medical event.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be preprinted or collected when the applicant needs to identify the specific side of the anatomical location. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier further detailing the position of the anatomical location, relative to the center of the body, organ, or specimen.
Variables.Question Text: What was the directionality of the anatomical location of the medical condition or event?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the directionality of the anatomical location of the medical event.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be preprinted or collected when the applicant needs to identify the directionality of the anatomical location. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: MH Event Location Portion or Totality
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier for anatomical location, further detailing the distribution (i.e., arrangement of, apportioning of).
Variables.Question Text: What was the portion or totality of the anatomical location of the of the medical condition or event?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate the portion or totality anatomical location of the medical event.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collected when the applicant needs to identify the specific portionality for the anatomical locations. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: If the value for MHTERM is modified to facilitate coding, then MHMODIFY will contain the modified text.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This is not a data collection field that would appear on the CRF. Applicants will populate this through the coding process.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary text description of MHTERM or the modified topic variable (MH MODIFY), if applicable.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This is typically not a data collection field that will appear on the CRF. Applicants will populate this through the coding process. Equivalent to the Preferred Term (PT in MedDRA).

Variables.Collection Variable Label: Medical History Event Lowest Level Term
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived text description of the lowest level term.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. Applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: MH Event Lowest Level Term Code
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived code for the lowest level term.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. Applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived code for the preferred term.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. Applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: Medical History Event High Level Term
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived text description of the high level term for the primary system organ class (SOC).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. Applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: MH Event High Level Term Code
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived code for the high level term for the primary system organ class (SOC).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. Applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: MH Event High Level Group Term
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived text description of the high level group term for the primary system organ class (SOC).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. Applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: MH Event High Level Group Term Code
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived code for the high level group term for the primary system organ class (SOC).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. Applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: MH Event Primary System Organ Class
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived text description of the primary system organ class (SOC).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. Applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding. Will be the same as MH BODSYS if the primary SOC was used for analysis.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: MH Event Primary System Organ Class Code
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The dictionary-derived code for the primary system organ class (SOC).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field does not typically appear on the CRF. Applicants will populate this through the coding process. This is applicable to items using MedDRA coding. Will be the same as MHBDSYCD if the primary SOC was used for analysis.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included into the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the subject identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system generated. This collection variable is typically collected in all collection domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The name of an encounter that encompasses planned and unplanned study interventions, procedures, and assessments that may be performed on a subject.
Variables.Question Text: What is the visit name?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The name of the clinical encounter is typically preprinted on the CRF or displayed in the EDC for any visit-based data collection, most often in Findings domains. This Visit text description is then available in any EDC data extract for that Findings domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Date the encounter occurred (or started).
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the date of the visit?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the [date/start date] of the visit using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field is not a tabulation variable. The date of a measurement, test, observation can be determined from the date/time of visit (VISDAT/VISTIM) and then concatenating the VISDAT/VISTIM components and populating the tabulation variable DADTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date the accountability assessments were collected can be determined from the Visit Date variable (VISDAT) and applying that date to all of the observations at that visit, or the collection date can be included on the DA CRF using the date (DADAT) field.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether a planned product accountability assessment was performed.
Variables.Question Text: Was product accountability performed?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate whether or not product accountability was performed.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. May be used to derive a value into the tabulation variable DASTAT. If DAPERF="N", the value of DASTAT will be "NOT DONE". If DAPERF="Y", DASTAT should be null. A combination of tabulation variables ( e.g., DACAT and DASCAT, DATPT) is used to indicate that multiple tests were not done. In this situation, the tabulation variable DATESTCD would be populated as DAALL and an appropriate test name (DATEST) provided.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This may be implemented on a CRF page level on a visit-by-visit basis. This general prompt question is used as a data management tool to verify that missing results are confirmed missing.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the type of product for which accountability was assessed?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the type of product dispensed/returned.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be preprinted on the CRF or screen and prepopulated in the data management system. This is not typically a question to which the site would provide an answer.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the DACAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the name of the product for which product accountability was assessed?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the name of the study product dispensed/returned.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be preprinted on the CRF or screen and prepopulated in the data management system. This is not typically a question to which the site would provide an answer. If known at the time of data collection, the product name may be collected in DASCAT (with appropriate grouping values, but different from those for DACAT). See tabulation DA domain examples for populating DACAT and DASCAT. DASCAT can only be used if there is an DACAT, and it must be a subcategorization of DACAT.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date the study product was dispensed or returned, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the date the product accountability assessment was performed?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the exact date the study product was (dispensed or returned), using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable DADTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date investigational product dispensed/returned should be recorded for each dispensation for a study with multiple periods or multiple products dispensed.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An internal or external identifier such as product label identifier.
Variables.Question Text: What was the product label identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record product label identifier.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: For the tabulation dataset, DAREFID should be used to tie together a block of related records and to link dispensed product to returned product. The packaging identifier may be collected in different ways (e.g., affixing label onto CRF, scanning a bar code). For some cases, greater granularity for product identifiers may be needed. In this situation, applicants may need to use additional identifier variables.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Descriptive name of the measurement or finding (e.g., dispensed, returned).
Variables.Question Text: What was the product accountability being assessed?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the name of the product accountability assessment if not preprinted on the CRF. If collected on the CRF, the applicant may provide additional instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation variable DATESTCD may be determined from the value collected in the collection field DATEST. The tabulation variables DATESTCD and DATEST are required in the tabulation datasets. Use appropriate CDISC Controlled Terminology for the test and test code.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Required to identify which test the result is for. It is recommended that the test names preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a field that requires the site to enter text. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Test" can be included as the column heading. For a study with multiple periods or multiple products dispensed, product accountability amounts should be assessed for each dispensation.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: DA Assessment Result in Original Units
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Result of the product accountability assessment as originally dispensed or returned (e.g., actual amount).
Variables.Question Text: What is the result of the product accountability assessment?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the actual amount of product dispensed or returned.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: For a study with multiple periods or multiple products dispensed, product accountability amounts should be assessed for each dispensation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit of the result as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What was the unit?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record or select the original units in which these data were collected, if not preprinted on CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Should be preprinted on the CRF with the associated test when possible, rather than collected in a free-text field.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included in the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system-generated. This collection variable is typically collected in all collection domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The name of an encounter that encompasses planned and unplanned study interventions, procedures, and assessments that may be performed on a subject.
Variables.Question Text: What is the visit name?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The name of the clinical encounter is typically preprinted on the CRF or displayed within the EDC for any visit-based data collection, most often in Findings domains. This Visit text description is then available in any EDC data extract for that Findings domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Date the encounter occurred (or started).
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the date of the visit?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the [date/start date] of the visit using theis format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field is not a tabulation variable. The date of a measurement, test, observation can be determined from the date/time of visit (VISDAT/VISTIM) and then concatenating the VISDAT/VISTIM components and populating the tabulation variable IEDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date the inclusion and exclusion assessments were collected can be determined from the visit date variable (VISDAT) and applying that date to all of the observations at that visit or the collection date can be included on the Inclusion/Exclusion CRF using the date (IEDAT) field.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Indication whether the subject met all the eligibility requirements for this study at the time the subject was enrolled.
Variables.Question Text: Were all eligibility criteria met?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record Yes if all eligibility criteria were met at the time the subject was enrolled. Record No if subject did not meet all criteria at the time the subject was enrolled.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to an tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The intent/purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring. It provides verification if all other fields on the CRF were deliberately left blank.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date of collection of the inclusion/exclusion criteria represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the date the eligibility criteria assessment was performed?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record complete date when the eligibility assessment was performed using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable IEDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A complete date is expected. The date of collection may be determined from the date of visit (VISDAT) and, if so, a separate assessment date field is not required.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping category to denote whether the protocol entry criterion being assessed is inclusion criteria or exclusion criteria.
Variables.Question Text: What was the category of the criterion?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Check the appropriate box to indicate whether the criterion exception was related to the subject's inclusion or exclusion.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: These categories have been defined in controlled terminology that must be used. Only records for criteria that are not met appear in the IE tabulation domain. IECAT must be populated. This criterion category may be collected on the CRF in a tick/checkbox format or it may be included as part of the criterion identification and mapped when the tabulation datasets are created.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the IECAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the subcategory of the criterion?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, the applicant provides instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, and not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Subcategory" can be included as the column heading. This can be used to distinguish criteria for a sub-study or to categorize the criterion as a major or minor exception.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unique identifier associated with the criterion that was the exception.
Variables.Question Text: What was the identifier of the inclusion criterion the subject did not meet or the exclusion criterion the subject met?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If the subject was not eligible, record the identifying code for each criterion that was an exception.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field is required to appear on the CRF, but may be null if there are no exceptions to the inclusion/exclusion criteria. The CRF should allow multiple exceptions to be recorded. Applicants may provide a list of inclusion/exclusion criteria and the unique identifying codes to the site. The list provided should be versioned/updated when the protocol changes and the criteria are changed. Applicants should use applicant-developed controlled terminology for IETESTCD.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Descriptive name of the inclusion or exclusion criterion that was the exception.
Variables.Question Text: What was the description of the inclusion criterion the subject did not meet or the exclusion criterion the subject met?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the description of the criterion, if not preprinted on the CRF. If collected on the CRF, the applicant may provide additional instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation variable IETESTCD may be determined from the value collected in IETEST. The tabulation variables IETESTCD and IETEST are required in the tabulation datasets.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicants could automatically populated the text in EDC systems when the criterion identifier is populated by the investigator. This can be verified by the PI to ensure the right exception identifier was selected.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of which inclusion criterion was not met or exclusion criterion was met.
Variables.Question Text: What is the result?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, the applicant provides instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This is only a data collection field when a complete list of inclusion and exclusion criteria are included on the CRF with Yes/No response options. If the applicant collects only the criteria that are not fulfilled, then, when an inclusion criterion is not met, IEORRES is mapped to "N" and when an exclusion criterion is met, IEORRES is mapped to "Y".

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column .
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included in the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the subject identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be provided to the site using a prepopulated list in the system. This collection variable is typically collected in all domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The name of an encounter that encompasses planned and unplanned trial interventions, procedures, and assessments that may be performed on a subject.
Variables.Question Text: What is the visit name?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The name of the clinical encounter is typically preprinted on the CRF or displayed in the EDC for any visit-based data collection, most often in Findings domains. This Visit text description is then available in any EDC data extract for that Findings domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Date the encounter occurred (or started).
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the date of the visit?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the [date/start date] of the visit using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field is not an tabulation variable. The date of a measurement, test, observation can be determined from the date/time of visit (VISDAT/VISTIM) and then concatenating the VISDAT/VISTIM components and populating the tabulation variable VSDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date the RE measurements were collected can be determined from the visit date variable (VISDAT) and applying that date to all of the observations at that visit, or the collection date can be included on the RE CRF using the Respiratory Assessments (REDAT) field.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether a planned measurement, test, observation or specimen was performed/collected.
Variables.Question Text: Was a respiratory assessment performed?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate whether or not a respiratory assessment was done.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field does not map directly to an tabulation variable. May be used to populate a value into the tabulation variable RESTAT. If the collection variable REPERF="N", the value of the tabulation variable RESTAT is "NOT DONE". If REPERF= "Y", RESTAT is null. A combination of tabulation variables (e.g., RECAT and RESCAT, RETPT) is used to indicate that multiple tests were not done. In this situation, the tabulation variable RETESTCD would be populated with REALL and an appropriate test name (RETEST) provided.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field is used to capture a response to whether or not a planned measurement, test or observation was performed. A negative response can be collected as "N" and mapped to the -STAT variable in SDTM as " NOT DONE".

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date the respiratory measurement was performed, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the date the respiratory measurement was taken?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record date of measurements using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field does not map directly to an tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable REDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date the RE measurements were collected can be determined from the visit date variable (VISDAT) and applying that date to all of the observations at that visit, or the collection date can be included on the RE CRF using the Date of Collection (REDAT) field.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The time of measurement, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the time of the respiratory system measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record time of measurement (as complete as possible).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field does not map directly to an tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable REDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A single collection time (e.g., RETIM) may be collected for all the measurements when they are performed at the same time. The time of each measurement can also be collected using a collection variable [RETESTCD]_RETIM.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: RE Assessment Planned Time Point Name
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A text description of planned timepoints when measurements should be taken, as defined in the protocol.
Variables.Question Text: What is the planned timepoint for this respiratory assessment measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the planned time-point labels for respiratory assessment, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation time-point anchors RETPTREF (text description) and RERFTDTC (date/time) may be needed, as well as tabulation variables RETPTNUM, REELTM.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Planned timepoints are needed to differentiate multiple sequential assessments. It is recommended that timepoints should be preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a free-text field. If the form is laid out as a grid, then terms such as "Planned Time Point" can be included in the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Descriptive name of the test or examination used to obtain the measurement or finding.
Variables.Question Text: What is the respiratory test name?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the name of the respiratory test, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation variable RETESTCD may be determined from the value collected in RETEST using the Controlled Terminology List RETESTCD.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The test name will usually be preprinted on the CRF, and not solicited as a question. If the form is laid out as a grid, then "Test" or "Test Name" can be included in the column heading. RETEST is most useful as the PROMPT on the field in which the RESULT for that test is collected.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What is the category of the respiratory test?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the respiratory assessment category, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be a heading on the CRF or screen, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. RESCAT can only be used if there is a RECAT. If a question is asked, the response would typically be an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Category" can be included in the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the RECAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the subcategory of the respiratory assessment?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the respiratory assessment subcategory, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Subcategory" can be included in the column heading. RESCAT can only be used if there is a RECAT, and it must be a subcategorization of RECAT.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: RE Test Result in Original Units
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Result of the measurement or finding as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What was the result of the measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the respiratory test result.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Both quantitative results and interpretive findings or summaries may be recorded here.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit of the result as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What was the unit of the result?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record or select the original unit in which these data were collected, if not preprinted on CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Should be preprinted on the CRF with the associated test when possible, rather than collected in a free-text field. Should be included if applicable and not available elsewhere.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The result of the measurement or finding as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: Was the result (normal/abnormal/absent/present/ [applicant defined response])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate the overall assessment for [RETEST].
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. The mapping instructions depend on the implementation; for example: \n 1. RERES is used to collect Normal, Abnormal or similar type classifications (e.g., Absent/Present) with a description of the abnormal result using the collection field REDESC. For tabulation datasets, If the collection field RERES = "NORMAL", populate the tabulation variables REORRES and RESTRESC with the value of the collection field RERES. If the collection field RERES is "ABNORMAL", populate the tabulation variable REORRES with the collection field REDESC. If the reported findings in REDESC are coded using a dictionary, then the tabulation variable RESTRESC is populated with the dictionary preferred term and REMODIFY is populated with the modified text used for coding. If the reported findings in REDESC are not coded, then the tabulation variable RESTRESC is populated with the collection REDESC field. The tabulation variable RENRIND may be populated with "NORMAL" or "ABNORMAL" if appropriate. \n 2. Where RERES is used to collect standardized values (e.g. a codelist) on the CRF and the value of "OTHER" is included, the collection field RERESOTH can be used to collect free-text values for "Specify Other". When using this field, the "OTHER" value recorded in the collect field RERES field is mapped to the tabulation variable RESTRESC and the value in the collection field RERESOTH is mapped to the tabulation variable REORRES.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The collection field RERES is used when the collected results are not mapped directly to the tabulation variable REORRES and must be transformed. For example,RERES is used to collect standardized values on the CRF and the value of "OTHER" is included and "Specify Other" is collected.REORES is collected using Normal, Abnormal and a description of the abnormality is collected.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Text description of respiratory test findings.
Variables.Question Text: What was the description of the (abnormality/observed finding/[Applicant-defined])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record all abnormal findings for the respiratory test in the space provided.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. May be used to populate a value into the tabulation variable REORRES. If RERES="Normal", populate REORRES with the value of RERES. If RERES="Abnormal", populate REORRES with the value of REDESC.
Variables.Implementation Notes: RERES and REDESC are used when a question is asked to collect the finding result, with a follow-up question for a description of the finding.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A free-text result which provides further information about the original received or collected result.
Variables.Question Text: If other is selected, [explain/specify/provide more detail].
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Provide more detail for the "Other" result.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: When using this collection field, the "OTHER" value collected in the collection field RERES is mapped to the tabulation variable RESTRESC and the value in the collection field RERESOTH is mapped to the tabulation variable REORRES.
Variables.Implementation Notes: In cases where RERES is used to collect standardized values on the CRF and the value of "OTHER" is included, the collection field RERESOTH can be used to collect free-text values for "Specify Other".

Variables.Collection Variable Label: RE Ref Range Lower Limit- Original Unit
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The lower end of normal range or reference range for continuous results stored in REORRES.
Variables.Question Text: What was the lower limit of the reference range?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the lower limit of the reference range of the respiratory test.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: REORNRLO should be populated only for continuous findings. The tabulation variable RESTNRC should be populated only for noncontinuous results. These data may be obtained from the lab or the electronic equipment. These data could be derived from a site or lab specific set of normal ranges stored in a look-up table.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: RE Ref Range Upper Limit- Original Unit
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The upper end of normal range or reference range for continuous results stored in REORRES.
Variables.Question Text: What was the upper limit of the reference range?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the upper limit of the reference range of the respiratory test.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: REORNRHI should be populated only for continuous findings. The tabulation variable RESTNRC should be populated only for noncontinuous results. These data may be obtained from the lab or the electronic equipment. These data could be derived from a site or lab specific set of normal ranges stored in a look-up table.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication or description about how the value compares to the normal range or reference range.
Variables.Question Text: How do the reported values compare within the [reference/normal/expected] range?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record where the test result fell with respect to the reference range.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Reference ranges may be defined by REORNRLO, REORNRHI, RESTNRC or other objective criteria. Reference Range Indicator (e.g., Y, N; HIGH, LOW; NORMAL, ABNORMAL) may be included if not derived or determined programmatically after data collection. Should not be used to indicate clinical significance.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: This variable is used to indicate that data are not available, by having the site recording the value as "Not Done".
Variables.Question Text: Indicate if the [RETEST] was not [answered/assessed/done/evaluated/performed].
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the respiratory assessment or measurement was not done.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Used only when the response value is collected as NOT DONE or NULL in lieu of or in addition to the collection REPERF field. Typically a checkbox which indicates the test was NOT DONE. This field can be useful when multiple questions are asked to confirm that a blank result field is meant to be blank.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An explanation for why the data are not available.
Variables.Question Text: Was the was the reason that the respiratory (assessment/[RETEST]) was not [collected / answered / done / assessed / evaluated]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Provide the reason the measurement or test was not done.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology may be used. The reason the data are not available may be chosen from an applicant-defined codelist (e.g., broken equipment, subject refused) or entered as free text. When REREASND is used, RESTAT should also be populated in the SDTM-based dataset.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The position of the subject during a measurement or examination.
Variables.Question Text: What was the position of the subject during the assessment?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the position of subject at time of test.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Results may be affected by whether conditions for respiratory test, as specified in the protocol, were properly met. One common condition is the subject's position. If the protocol requires this type of information, then a collection variable [RETESTCD]_REPOS may be created for each RETESTCD and added to the CRF, if needed.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Location used for the measurement.
Variables.Question Text: What was the anatomical location where the measurement was taken?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record or select location on body where the measurement was performed.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collected or preprinted when the applicant needs to identify the specific anatomical location. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.LAT, DIR, and PORTOT are used to further describe the anatomical location.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier for anatomical location, further detailing the side of the body.
Variables.Question Text: What was the side of the anatomical location of the [measurement/test/examination])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the side of the anatomical location of the respiratory test or measurement.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be preprinted or collected when the applicant needs to identify the specific side of the anatomical location. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier further detailing the position of the anatomical location, relative to the center of the body, organ, or specimen.
Variables.Question Text: What was the directionality of the anatomical location of the respiratory test?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the directionality of the anatomical location of the respiratory test.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be preprinted or collected when the applicant needs to identify the directionality of the anatomical location. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The method of the test or examination.
Variables.Question Text: What was the method (used for the [measurement/test/examination])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the method used for the respiratory test.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This information may be collected when more than 1 method is possible, and collecting the method used is necessary.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The role of the person who provided the evaluation.
Variables.Question Text: Who was the evaluator?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Select the role of the person who provided the evaluation.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Used only for results that are subjective (e.g., assigned by a person or a group). May be a preprinted or collected. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An identifier used to distinguish multiple evaluators with the same role recorded in REEVAL.
Variables.Question Text: What is the identifier of the evaluator?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the unique identifier assigned to the person making the evaluation.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collect if multiple evaluators are used in the study (may be omitted if multiple evaluators are not used); values should follow controlled terminology.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication that the evaluation is considered, by an independent assessor, to be the accepted or final evaluation.
Variables.Question Text: Was this record considered to be the accepted evaluation?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate whether or not the evaluation is considered, by an independent assessor, to be the accepted or final evaluation.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Use where more than one assessor provides an evaluation of a result or response. Typically a checkbox with the value of "Y" or "NULL", which indicates the evaluation was accepted.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The instance number of a test that is repeated within a given timeframe for the same test. The level of granularity can vary (e.g., within a timepoint, within a visit).
