Variables.Question Text: What was the repetition number within the timepoint for this measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the repetition number of the measurement within the timepoint.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPRE dataset as the value of SUPPRE.QVAL where SUPPRE.QNAM = "REREPNUM" and SUPPRE.QLABEL= "Repetition Number within Time Point".
Variables.Implementation Notes: The repetition number of the test/measurement within the timepoint may be preprinted on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether the test results were clinically significant.
Variables.Question Text: Was this result clinically significant?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether respiratory test results were clinically significant.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPRE dataset as the value of SUPPRE.QVAL when SUPPRE.QNAM = "CLSIG" and SUPPRE.QLABEL = "Clinical Significance".
Variables.Implementation Notes: Could apply to specific measurements or to overall interpretation, as required by the protocol.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included in the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper-This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC- The subject identifiers may be provided to the site using a prepopulated list in the system. This collection variable is typically collected in all domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The name of an encounter that encompasses planned and unplanned study interventions, procedures, and assessments that may be performed on a subject.
Variables.Question Text: What is the visit name?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The name of the clinical encounter is typically preprinted on the CRF or displayed within the EDC for any visit-based data collection, most often in Findings domains. This Visit text description is then available in any EDC data extract for that Findings domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Date the encounter occurred (or started).
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the date of the visit?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the [date/start date] of the visit using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field is not a tabulation variable. The date of a measurement, test, observation can be determined from the date/time of visit (VISDAT/VISTIM) and then concatenating the collection VISDAT/VISTIM components and populating the tabulation variable SCDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date the subject characteristics were collected can be determined from the visit date variable (VISDAT) and applying that date to all of the subject characteristics at that visit, or the collection date can be included on the SC CRF using the date (SCDAT) field.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the category of the subject characteristics?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the subject characteristics category, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Category" can be included in the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the SCCAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the subcategory of the subject characteristics?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the subject characteristics subcategory, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be a applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Subcategory" can be included in the column heading. SCSCAT can only be used if there is an SCCAT, and it must be a subcategorization of SCCAT.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether any subject characteristics were collected.
Variables.Question Text: Were subject characteristics collected?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if subject characteristics information was collected. If Yes, record the appropriate details.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. May be used to derive a value into the tabulation variable SCSTAT. If SCPERF="N", the value of SCSTAT will be "NOT DONE" . If SCPERF="Y", SCSTAT should be null. A combination of tabulation variables (e.g., SCCAT and SCSCAT, SCTPT) is used to indicate that multiple tests were not done. In this situation, the tabulation variable SCTESTCD would be populated as SCALL and an appropriate test name (SCTEST) provided.
Variables.Implementation Notes: General prompt question to be used as a data management tool to verify that missing results are confirmed missing.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An applicant-defined identifier. This is typically used for preprinted or auto-generated numbers on the CRF, or any other type of identifier that does not already have a defined collection identifier field.
Variables.Question Text: [Applicant-defined question]
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, the applicant may insert instructions to ensure each record has a unique identifier.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Because SPID is a applicant-defined identifier, conformance to Question Text or Item Prompt is not applicable. Typically used as an identifier in a data query to communicate clearly to the site the specific record in question or to reconcile data. May be used to record preprinted number (e.g., line number, record number) on the CRF. This field may be populated by the applicant's data collection system.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date of collection represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the date the subject characteristics were collected?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the date the subject characteristics were collected using the format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected collection DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable SCDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date of collection can be determined from a collected date of the visit (VISDAT); in such cases, a date field is not required.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Descriptive name of the subject characteristic of interest.
Variables.Question Text: What is the subject characteristics name?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the name of the subject characteristics if not preprinted on the CRF. If collected on the CRF, the applicant may provide additional instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation variable SCTESTCD may be determined from the value collected in SCTEST. Use appropriate CDISC Controlled Terminology for the test and test code.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Required to identify which test the result is for. It is recommended that the test names be preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a free-text field. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Test" can be included in the column header.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: SC Result or Finding in Original Units
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Result of the subject characteristic as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What is the subject characteristic?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the subject characteristic.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included in the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the subject identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be provided to the site using a prepopulated list in the system. This collection variable is typically collected in all collection domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The name of an encounter that encompasses planned and unplanned study interventions, procedures, and assessments that may be performed on a subject.
Variables.Question Text: What is the visit name?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The name of the clinical encounter is typically preprinted on the CRF or displayed within the EDC for any visit-based data collection, most often in Findings domains. This Visit text description is then available in any EDC data extract for that Findings domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Date the encounter occurred (or started).
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the date of the visit?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the [date/start date] of the visit using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field is not an tabulation variable. The date of a measurement, test, observation can be determined from the date/time of visit (VISDAT/VISTIM) and then concatenating the VISDAT/VISTIM components and populating the tabulation variable VSDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date the VS measurements were collected can be determined from the visit date variable (VISDAT) and applying that date to all of the observations at that visit, or the collection date can be included on the VS CRF using the Vital Signs Date (VSDAT) field.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether a planned vital signs measurement, series of vital signs measurements, tests, or observations was performed.
Variables.Question Text: Were vital signs performed?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if vital signs were collected. If Yes, include the appropriate details where indicated on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. May be used to derive a value into the tabulation variable VSSTAT. If VSPERF="N", the value of VSSTAT will be "NOT DONE". If VSPERF="Y", VSSTAT should be null. A combination of tabulation variables (e.g., VSCAT and VSSCAT, VSTPT) is used to indicate that multiple tests were not done. In this situation, the tabulation variable VSTESTCD would be populated as VSALL and an appropriate test name VSTEST provided.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This general prompt question is used as a data management tool to verify that missing results are confirmed missing.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date of the vital signs measurement, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the date of the vital signs measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record date of measurements using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable VSDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date of measurement can be determined from a collected date of visit (VISDAT); in such cases, a separate measurement date field is not required.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The time of measurement, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the time of the vital signs measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record time of measurement (as complete as possible).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable VSDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collect time if it is relevant for the analysis.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An applicant-defined identifier. This is typically used for preprinted or auto-generated numbers on the CRF, or any other type of identifier that does not already have a defined identifier field.
Variables.Question Text: [Applicant-defined question]
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, the applicant may insert instructions to ensure each record has a unique identifier.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. May be used to create RELREC to link this record with a record in another domain.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Because SPID is an applicant-defined identifier, conformance to Question Text or Item Prompt is not applicable. Typically used as an identifier in a data query to communicate clearly to the site the specific record in question or to reconcile data. May be used to record preprinted number (e.g. line number, record number) on the CRF. This field may be populated by the applicant's data collection system.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: Vital Signs Planned Time Point Name
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A text description of planned timepoints when measurements should be taken, as defined in the protocol.
Variables.Question Text: What is the planned timepoint for this vital signs measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the planned time-point labels for vital signs, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation time-point anchors VSTPTREF (text description) and VSRFTDTC (date/time) may be needed, as well as tabulation variables VSTPTNUM, VSELTM.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Planned timepoints are needed to differentiate multiple sequential assessments. It is recommended that timepoints should be preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a free-text field. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Planned Time Point" can be included in the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the category of the vital signs?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the vital signs category, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This is most commonly either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be from a applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Category" can be included in the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the VSCAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the subcategory of the vital signs?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the vital signs subcategory, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This is most commonly either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be a applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Subcategory" can be included in the column heading. VSSCAT can only be used if there is a VSCAT, and it must be a subcategorization of VSCAT.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The instance number of a test that is repeated within a given timeframe for the same test. The level of granularity can vary (e.g., within a timepoint, within a visit).
Variables.Question Text: What was the repetition number within the timepoint for this measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the repetition number of the measurement within the timepoint.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPVS dataset as the value of SUPPVS.QVAL where SUPPVS.QNAM= "VSREPNUM" and SUPPVS.QLABEL= "Repetition Number within timepoint".
Variables.Implementation Notes: The repetition number of the test/measurement within the timepoint may be preprinted on the CRF (e.g., multiple measurements of blood pressure, multiple analyses of a sample).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Descriptive name of the test or examination used to obtain the measurement or finding.
Variables.Question Text: What is the vital sign test name?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the name of the vital sign test if not preprinted on the CRF. If collected on the CRF, the applicant may provide additional instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation variable VSTESTCD may be determined from the value collected in VSTEST. Both VSTESTCD and VSTEST are required in the tabulation datasets. Use appropriate CDISC Controlled Terminology for the test and test code.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Required to identify which test the result is for. It is recommended that test names be preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a free-text field. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Test" can be included in the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: This variable is used to indicate that data are not available, by having the site recording the value as "Not Done".
Variables.Question Text: Indicate if the vital signs measurement was not done
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the vital sign measurement was not done.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A Not Done checkbox, which indicates the test was NOT DONE. Typically, there would be 1 checkbox for each measurement. This field can be useful on individual VS tests to confirm that a blank result field is meant to be blank.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: VS Result or Finding in Original Units
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Result of the vital signs measurement as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What was the result of the measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the vital sign result.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit of the result as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What was the unit of the measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record or select the original unit in which these data were collected, if not preprinted on CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This should be preprinted on the CRF (or enterable from a picklist) with the associated test when possible, rather than collected as free-text.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication whether the vital sign result was clinically significant.
Variables.Question Text: Was the result clinically significant?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether the vital sign result was clinically significant.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPVS dataset as the value of SUPPVS.QVAL where SUPPVS.QNAM = "VSCLSIG" and SUPPVS.QLABEL="Clinically Significant".

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A description of the anatomical location of the subject, relevant to the collection of vital signs measurements.
Variables.Question Text: What was the anatomical location where the measurement was taken?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record or select location on body where measurement was performed, if not preprinted on CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collected or preprinted when the applicant needs to identify the specific anatomical location (e.g., ARM for blood pressure). Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF. LAT, DIR, and PORTOT are used to further describe the anatomical location.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The position of the subject during a measurement or examination.
Variables.Question Text: What was the position of the subject during the measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the position of subject at time of test (e.g., SITTING).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Results may be affected by whether conditions for vital signs, as specified in the protocol, were properly met. One common condition is the subject's position.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier further detailing the position of the anatomical location, relative to the center of the body, organ, or specimen.
Variables.Question Text: What was the directionality of the anatomical location of the measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the directionality.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be preprinted or collected when the applicant needs to identify the directionality of the anatomical location. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier for anatomical location, further detailing the side of the body.
Variables.Question Text: What was the side of the anatomical location of the vital signs measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the side of the anatomical location of the vital signs measurement.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be preprinted or collected when the applicant needs to identify the specific side of the anatomical location. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included in the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system-generated. This collection variable is typically collected in all domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The name of an encounter that encompasses planned and unplanned trial interventions, procedures, and assessments that may be performed on a subject.
Variables.Question Text: What is the visit name?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The name of the clinical encounter is typically preprinted or displayed within the EDC for any visit-based data collection, most often in Findings domains. This Visit text description is then available in any EDC data extract for that Findings domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Date the encounter occurred (or started).
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the date of the visit?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the [date/start date] of the visit using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field is not an tabulation variable. The date of a measurement, test, observation, or specimen collection can be determined from the date/time of visit (VISDAT/VISTIM) and then concatenating the collection VISDAT/VISTIM components and populating the tabulation variable FADTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date the finding about measurements were collected can be determined from the visit date variable (VISDAT) and applying that date to all of the observations at that visit, or the collection date can be included on the FA CRF using the Findings About Date (FADAT) field.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: Findings About Object of the Observation
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A description of the object or focal point of the findings observation that is represented by FATEST.
Variables.Question Text: [Applicantsdt,-defined phrase]
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: [Protocol-specific]
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The FAOBJ will usually be preprinted or hidden, not solicited as an actual question. These FA domains are usually created by the applicant.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether data was collected for the finding topic.
Variables.Question Text: Has the subject had any [Findings topic(s)] (after/before [study specific time frame])?; [Was/Were] (there) any [Findings topic(s)] (reported) (after/before [study specific time frame])?; Were all eligibility criteria met?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the there are findings. If Yes, include the appropriate details where indicated on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to a tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This is a field that can be used in any CRF to indicate whether there is data to record. Used primarily as a data cleaning field, it provides verification that all other fields on the CRF were deliberately left blank. FAPERF should be used to capture a response about whether planned measurements, tests, or observations were done.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether a planned measurement, series of measurements, test, observation or specimen was performed or collected.
Variables.Question Text: [Were any/Was the] [FATEST/topic] ([measurement(s)/test(s)/examination(s)/specimen(s)/sample(s))] [performed/collected]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the [FATESTs] was/were collected. If Yes, include the appropriate details where indicated on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field does not map directly to an tabulation variable. May be used to populate a value into the tabulation variable FASTAT. If the collection variable FAPERF="N", the value of the tabulation variable FASTAT is "OT DONE". If FAPERF="Y", FASTAT is null. A combination of tabulation variables (e.g., FACAT and FASCAT, FATPT) is used to indicate that multiple tests were not done. In this situation, the tabulation variable FATESTCD would be populated with FAALL and an appropriate test name (FATEST) provided.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This field is used to capture a response to whether a planned measurement, test or observation was performed. A negative response can be collected as "N" and mapped to the tabulation FASTAT variable as "NOT DONE".

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date when the findings about assessment was performed, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the date the findings about assessment was performed?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record date of measurements using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable FADTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date the FA measurements were collected can be determined from the visit date variable (VISDAT) and applying that date to all of the observations at that visit, or the collection date can be included on the FA CRF using the Date of Collection (FADAT) field.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The time of measurement, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the time of the findings about assessment?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record time of measurement (as complete as possible).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable VSDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collect time if it is relevant for the analysis.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Descriptive name for the test being performed.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the name (of the [measurement/test/examination])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the name of the FATEST if not preprinted on the CRF. If collected on the CRF, the applicant may provide additional instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation variable FATESTCD may be determined from the value collected in FATEST.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Required to identify which test the result is for. It is recommended that the test names be preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a free-text field. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Test" can be included in the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A further description of FATESTCD and FATEST.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the [measurement/test/examination] detail name?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the detail of the [FATEST], if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: It is recommended that the test detail name be preprinted on the CRF. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Test," "Test Name" can be included in the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the [type/category/name] (of the [measurement/test/examination/specimen/sample])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the FA category, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This is most commonly either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be a applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Category" can be included in the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the FACAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the [type/subcategory/name] (of the [measurement/test/examination/specimen/sample])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the FA subcategory, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This is most commonly either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be a applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Subcategory" can be included in the column heading. FASCAT can only be used if there is an FACAT, and it must be a subcategorization of FACAT.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The position of the subject during a measurement or examination.
Variables.Question Text: In what position was the subject during the [measurement/ test/examination/specimen collection/sample collection]?; What was the position of the subject (during the [measurement/test/examination/specimen collection/sample collection])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the position of the subject during the FA test.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: FA Result or Finding in Original Units
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Result of the measurement or finding as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the [result/amount/(subject's) characteristic] (of the [measurement/test/examination/question/assessment])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the FATEST result.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Both quantitative results and interpretive findings or summaries may be recorded here.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit of the result as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the unit (of the [measurement/test/examination])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Select the unit of measure associated with the test, or record if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Should be preprinted on the CRF with the associated test when possible, rather than collected in a free-text field. Should be included if applicable and not available elsewhere.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: FA Normal Range Lower Limit- Orig Unit
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The lower end of normal range or reference range for continuous results stored in FAORRES.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the lower limit of the reference range (for the [measurement/test/examination])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the lower limit of the reference range of the FA test.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: --ORNRLO should be populated only for continuous findings. The tabulation variable --STNRC should be populated only for noncontinuous results. These data may be obtained from the lab or the electronic equipment, or could be derived from a site- or lab-specific set of normal ranges stored in a look-up table.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: FA Normal Range Upper Limit- Orig Unit
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The upper end of normal range or reference range for continuous results stored in FAORRES.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the upper limit of the reference range (for the [measurement/test/examination])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the upper limit of the reference range of the FA test.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: --ORNRHI should be populated only for continuous findings. The tabulation variable --STNRC should be populated only for noncontinuous results. These data may be obtained from the lab or the electronic equipment, or could be derived from a site- or lab-specific set of normal ranges stored in a look-up table.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication or description about how the value compares to the normal range or reference range.
Variables.Question Text: How [did/do] the reported values compare within the [reference/normal/expected] range?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record where the test results were categorized within the respective reference range (e.g. HIGH, LOW, ABNORMAL).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Reference ranges may be defined by FAORNRLO, FAORNRHI, FASTNRC or other objective criteria. Reference Range Indicator may be included if not derived or determined programmatically after data collection. Should not be used to indicate clinical significance.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: This variable is used to indicate that data are not available, by having the site recording the value as "Not Done".
Variables.Question Text: Was the [--TEST ] not [completed/answered/done/assessed/evaluated ]?; Indicate if the([--TEST] was) not [answered/assessed/done/evaluated/performed].
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the [FATEST] measurement was not done.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Used only when the response value is collected as NOT DONE or NULL in lieu of or in addition to the collection FAPERF field. Typically a checkbox which indicates the test was NOT DONE. This field can be useful when multiple questions are asked to confirm that a blank result field is meant to be blank.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An explanation of why data are not available.
Variables.Question Text: Was the [is/was] the reason that the [Findings topic/data/information/applicant-defined phrase] was not [collected/answered/done/assessed/evaluated]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Provide the reason why an FA test was not collected.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology may be used. The reason the data are not available may be chosen from applicant defined codelist (e.g., broken equipment, subject refused) or entered as free text. When --REASND is used, --STAT should also be populated in the tabulation dataset.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The type of specimen used for a measurement.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the specimen type?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the specimen material type.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The type of specimen used for a measure. Should be collected if not available elsewhere, or if required to differentiate multiple specimens.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Description of the condition of the specimen.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the condition of the specimen?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the condition of the specimen.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be collected using free or standardized text. Results may be affected by whether conditions for specimen were properly met. When local processing is used, applicants may not routinely collect specimen condition.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The anatomical location of the subject, relevant to the collection of the measurement.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the anatomical location (of the [measurement/test/examination]) or What [is/was] the anatomical location where the [measurement/specimen] was taken/collected)?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record or select location on body where the measurement was performed, if not preprinted on CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collected or preprinted when the applicant needs to identify the specific anatomical location (e.g., ARM for blood pressure). Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF. LAT, DIR, and PORTOT are used to further describe the anatomical location.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: Laterality of Location of Finding About
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier for anatomical location, further detailing the side of the body.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the side (of the anatomical location of the [measurement/test/examination])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the side of the anatomical location of the [FATEST] measurement.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be preprinted or collected when the applicant needs to identify the specific side of the anatomical location. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier further detailing the position of the anatomical location, relative to the center of the body, organ, or specimen.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the directionality (of the anatomical location of the [measurement/test/examination])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the directionality.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be preprinted or collected when the applicant needs to identify the directionality of the anatomical location. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier for anatomical location, further detailing the distribution (i.e.,arrangement of, apportioning of).
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the portion or totality (of the anatomical location of the [measurement/test/examination])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate the portion or totality anatomical location.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collected when the applicant needs to identify the specific portionality for the anatomical locations of the location of the FATEST. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Method of the test or examination.
Variables.Question Text: What was the method (used for the [measurement/test/examination])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the method used for the measurement, test, or examination.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The lead or leads identified to capture the measurement for a test from an instrument.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the lead (used to measure [measurement/test/examination])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the lead used for measurement.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication that the subject has abstained from food/water for the specified amount of time.
Variables.Question Text: [Is/Was] the subject fasting (prior to the [test being performed/sample being collected])?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether the subject was fasting prior to the test being performed.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Results may be affected by whether the subject was fasting. This may not be relevant for all tests.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The role of the person providing the evaluation.
Variables.Question Text: Who provided the (applicant-defined phrase) information?; Who was the evaluator?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Select the role of the person who provided the evaluation (e.g., INVESTIGATOR, VENDOR).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Used only for results that are subjective (e.g., assigned by a person or a group). May be a preprinted, or collected. Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An identifier used to distinguish multiple evaluators with the same role recorded in FAEVAL.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the identifier of the [evaluator name/reporter name] (providing the-applicant-defined phrase-information)?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the unique identifier assigned to the person making the evaluation.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This variable is used in conjunction with FAEVAL to provide an additional level of detail.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication whether the test results were clinically significant.
Variables.Question Text: [Is/Was] the ([measurement/test/examination]) result clinically significant?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether the [FATEST] result was clinically significant.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPFA dataset as the value of SUPPFA.QVAL when SUPPFA.QNAM = "CLSIG" and SUPPFA.QLABEL = "Clinical Significance".

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included in the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system-generated. This collection variable is typically collected in all domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A categorization of the disposition events, which is used to distinguish between disposition events, protocol milestones, and other events.
Variables.Question Text: What was the category of the disposition?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, the applicant provides instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This would most commonly be a heading on the CRF or screen, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. In this implementation scenario, DSCAT="PROTOCOL MILESTONE" or "OTHER EVENT".

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the DSCAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the subcategory of the disposition?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, the applicant provides instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be preprinted on the CRF or screen and prepopulated in the data management system. This is not typically a question to which the site would provide an answer. DSSCAT can only be used if there is an DSCAT and it must be a subcategorization of the Protocol Milestone or Other Event.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Trial Epoch (e.g., 'SCREENING', 'RUN-IN') for which subject disposition is being collected.
Variables.Question Text: What is the trial period for this disposition event?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Check the [epoch, or insert more appropriate wording] for which disposition event is being recorded.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: If protocol milestones or other events are collected more than once in the study, EPOCH may be needed to differentiate them. Typically, the trial epoch will be preprinted on the CRF as part of the title of the page; however, some companies have a standard CRF module that includes a pick-list of epochs.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The standardized terminology of the disposition term.
Variables.Question Text: [Applicant-defined]
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, the applicant provides instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. Both DSDECOD and DSTERM must be populated in the tabulation dataset.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Where DSCAT = "PROTOCOL MILESTONE", DSTERM contains the verbatim (as collected) and/or standardized text; DSDECOD uses the extensible controlled terminology codelist (PROTMLST). Where DSCAT="OTHER EVENT", DSDECOD uses the extensible controlled terminology codelist (OTHEVENT).

Variables.Collection Variable Label: Reported Term for the Disposition Event
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The verbatim or prespecified name of the disposition term.
Variables.Question Text: [Applicant-defined]
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, the applicant provides instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation variables DSDECOD and DSTERM must be populated in the tabulation dataset.
Variables.Implementation Notes: When defining protocol milestones or other events, applicants may populate DSTERM and DSDECOD with the same value (e.g., INFORMED CONSENT OBTAINED). DSTERM may also be populated with a verbatim term, which is then standardized in DSDECOD.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date of the specified protocol milestone (e.g., informed consent) represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the [protocol milestone/other event name] (start) date?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the date of the protocol milestone/other event as defined in the protocol and/or CRF completion instructions, using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable DSSTDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicants should define in the protocol and/or CRF completion instructions the criteria for completion of each protocol milestone/other event and its associated (start) date.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The time of the specified protocol milestone (e.g., informed consent) or other event, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the [protocol milestone/other event name] (start) time?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the time (as complete as possible) as defined in the protocol and/or CRF completion instructions.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable DSSTDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicants should define in the protocol and/or CRF completion instructions the criteria for completion of each protocol milestone/other event (start) time. Collecting the time of the event is only appropriate if it can be realistically determined and if there is a scientific reason for needing to know this level of detail.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included into the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.

Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system-generated. This collection variable is typically collected in all domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A categorization of the disposition events which is used to distinguish between disposition events, protocol milestones, and other events.
Variables.Question Text: What was the category of the disposition?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, the applicant provides instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This would most commonly be a heading on the CRF or screen, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. This is used to distinguish a DISPOSITION EVENT, a PROTOCOL MILESTONE, or an OTHER EVENT. In this implementation scenario, DSCAT="DISPOSITION EVENT"

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the DSCAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the subcategory of the disposition?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: If collected on the CRF, the applicant provides instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be preprinted on the CRF or screen and prepopulated in the data management system. This is not typically a question to which the site would provide an answer. DSSCAT can only be used if there is an DSCAT, and it must be a subcategorization of the Disposition event.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Trial epoch (e.g., 'SCREENING', 'RUN-IN') for which subject disposition is being collected.
Variables.Question Text: What is the trial period for this disposition event?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Check the [epoch, or insert more appropriate wording] for which disposition is being recorded.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: If disposition events are collected more than once in the study, EPOCH may be needed to differentiate them. Typically, the trial epoch will be preprinted on the CRF as part of the title of the page; however, some companies have a standard CRF module that includes a pick-list of epochs.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The standardized terminology of the disposition term that describes whether a subject completed the study or a portion of a study (epoch), or the reason they did not complete.
Variables.Question Text: What was the subject's status (at the EPOCH/study specific time frame)?
Variables.Prompt: Status (at the EPOCH/study specific time frame)
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Document the subject's status at [insert text corresponding to the selected trial epoch/study specific time frame]. If the subject discontinued prematurely, record the primary reason for discontinuation.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. Both DSDECOD and DSTERM must be populated in the tabulation datasets. If DSTERM was collected as an "Other, Specify" free text, populate DSTERM with the free text and populate DSDECOD with the applicant-defined standardized text. If DSDECOD was collected with no free text, populate DSTERM and DSDECOD in the tabulation dataset with the DSDECOD value that was collected.
Variables.Implementation Notes: DSDECOD can be used as the standardized coded list with DSTERM used to capture any "Specify, Other" information, or DSDECOD can be used on its own. For applicant- and/or study-specific reasons for discontinuation, it is recommended that these reasons be preprinted on the CRF, as subcategories of the appropriate standardized DSDECOD item. However, it is recommended to limit the use of applicant and study-specific reasons in order to promote consistent use of terminology and permit the combination of data across multiple applicants. Either DSTERM or DSDECOD must be on the CRF. Both may be used if DSTERM is used as a Specify, Other field.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: Reported Term for the Disposition Event
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The verbatim or prespecified name of the event. The reported or prespecified name for how a subject completed the study or a portion of a study (epoch), or the reason they did not complete.
Variables.Question Text: What was the subject's status?; If [DSDECOD], specify
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Document the subject's status at [insert text corresponding to the selected trial epoch]. If the subject discontinued prematurely, record the primary reason for discontinuation. (Or, if used with a DECOD list) If Other is selected from the Status list, provide the verbatim reason.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation variables DSDECOD and DSTERM must be populated in the tabulation dataset. If DSTERM was collected as an "Other, Specify" free text, populate the tabulation variable DSTERM with the free text and populate DSDECOD with the applicant-defined standardized text. If DSDECOD was collected with no free text, populate DSTERM and DSDECOD in the tabulation dataset with the DSDECOD value that was collected.
Variables.Implementation Notes: If used with a DECOD list, free-text description of the subject's "Other" status. DSTERM is the verbatim term for subject status when Other is selected from the DSDECOD code list. This field would only be used with the prompt and completion instructions provided as a Specify, Other field in conjunction with DSDECOD. DSTERM may be used by itself when no code list is provided for DSDECOD on the CRF. Either DSTERM or DSDECOD must be on the CRF. DSTERM is required in the tabulation dataset.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date of the specified disposition event (e.g., study completion or discontinuation), represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the disposition event date?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the date of disposition event as defined in the protocol and/or CRF completion instructions using this format (DD-MON-YYYY)
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable DSSTDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicants should define in the protocol and/or CRF completion instructions the criteria for completion of each epoch for which a Disposition CRF will be provided. Define also the date of completion or discontinuation. Only collect the date of the disposition event once.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The time of the specified disposition event (e.g., study completion or discontinuation), represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the disposition event time?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the time (as complete as possible) that the subject completed the study or portion of the study as defined in the protocol and/or CRF completion instructions. If the subject did not complete the study or portion of the study, record the time (as complete as possible) as defined in the protocol and/or CRF completion instructions.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected START DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable DSSTDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicants should define in the protocol and/or CRF completion instructions the criteria for completion of each epoch for which a Disposition CRF will be provided. Define also the date of completion or discontinuation. Collecting the time of completion or discontinuation is only appropriate if it can be realistically determined and if there is a scientific reason for needing to know this level of detail. Typically, it is not recommended that a time be collected unless the subject is under the direct care of the site at the time of the event. Only collect the time of completion or discontinuation on the Disposition CRF module if the same information is not being collected on another CRF module.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Date of death for any subject who died.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the subject's date of death?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the date of death
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field does not map directly to an tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable DTHDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The CDASH model defines Death Date as a timing variable; this is not included as a timing variable in the SDTM. It may be collected on any CRF deemed appropriate by the applicant, but should only be collected once. The tabulation variable DTHDTC is mapped to the DM domain during the tabulation dataset creation process. The tabulation variable DM.DTHFLG is not a collection variable, but is populated during the tabulation dataset creation process. Death Date may also be mapped to other tabulation domains (e.g., DS) as deemed appropriate by the applicant.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The plan for subject continuation to the next phase of the study or another study at the time of completion of the CRF.
Variables.Question Text: Will the subject continue?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record if the subject will be continuing to [the next phase of this study/related study] (applicant to specify as appropriate).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This information could be represented in a SUPPDS dataset as the value of SUPPDS.QVAL when SUPPDS.QNAM= "DSCONT" and SUPPDS.QLABEL="Subject Continue".
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicants should specify the next phase of the study or the related study on the CRF. Typically this is a prompt to aid in monitoring and data cleaning, and usually not represented in a SUPPDS dataset.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Identifies the study epoch or new study in which the subject will participate.
Variables.Question Text: What is the next [epoch/period/study/trial] the subject will [continue to/enter/enroll]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the planned subsequent [study epoch/study] in which the subject intends to participate.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Applicant-defined tabulation mapping.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicants should specify the next phase of the study or the related study on the CRF. The data are to be used to aid in monitoring and data cleaning. No specific tabulation dataset mapping rules are provided because the mapping depends on the situation (e.g., next epoch, next trial). Per applicant decision, plans to enter the next epoch within a study may be included in the tabulation datasets (e.g., SE). Actual subject entry into the next study is represented as part of Trial Design datasets of that study.

Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included in the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
