Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system-generated.This variable collection is typically collected in all collection domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The name of a clinical encounter that encompasses planned and unplanned study interventions, procedures, and assessments that may be performed on a subject.
Variables.Question Text: What is the visit name?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column..
Variables.Implementation Notes: The name of the clinical encounter is typically preprinted on the CRF or displayed within the EDC for any visit-based data collection, most often in Findings domains. This Visit text description is then available in any EDC data extract for that Findings domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Date the clinical encounter occurred (or started).
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the date of the visit?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the [date/start date] of the visit using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field is not a tabulation variable. The date of a measurement, test, observation can be determined from the date/time of visit (VISDAT/VISTIM) and then concatenating the VISDAT/VISTIM components and populating the tabulation variable DADTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date the accountability assessments were collected can be determined from the Visit Date variable (VISDAT) and applying that date to all of the observations at that visit, or the collection date can be included on the DA CRF using the date (DADAT) field.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An applicant-defined identifier used to tie a block of related records in a single domain.
Variables.Question Text: What is the test group identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record unique group identifier. Applicant may insert additional instructions to ensure each record has a unique group identifier.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: It can be beneficial to use an identifier in a data query to communicate clearly to the site the specific record in question. This group identifier ties together all the tests collected on this horizontal record. This field may be populated by the applicant's data collection system.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether a planned product accountability assessment was performed.
Variables.Question Text: Was [DATEST] collected?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate whether or not product accountability was performed.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. May be used to derive a value into the tabulation variable DASTAT. If DAPERF="N", the value of DASTAT will be "NOT DONE". If DAPERF="Y", DASTAT should be null. A combination of tabulation variables ( e.g., DACAT and DASCAT, DATPT) is used to indicate that multiple tests were not done. In this situation, the tabulation variable DATESTCD would be populated as DAALL and an appropriate test name (DATEST) provided.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This general prompt question is used as a data management tool to verify that missing results are confirmed missing. This may be implemented for all tests collected on the same horizontal record or for each specific test. When mapped to the tabulation dataset, the value of DAPERF would apply to all tests on the same record. Use the collection variable [DATESTCD]_DAPERF when implemented on a specific test basis. This is an example of the type of collection variable names that can be used in a denormalized data structure.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the type of product for which accountability was assessed?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the type of study product for which accountability is assessed.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. If the protocol allows dispensing different types of study product the CRF can capture the type of product using DACAT. This may be preprinted on the CRF. If DACAT is not collected (e.g., it is evident from the protocol design), it could be populated during the tabulation dataset creation process. The value of DACAT would apply to all measurements on that record when mapped to the tabulation dataset. If needed, the collection variable [DATESTCD]_DACAT may be used to collect a category for each DATEST.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the DACAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the name of the product for which accountability was assessed?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the name of the study product dispensed.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a category value preprinted on the CRF, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be a applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Subcategory" can be included as the column header. If known at the time of data collection, the product name may be collected in DASCAT (with appropriate grouping values, but different from those for DACAT). The value of DASCAT would apply to all measurements on that record when mapped to the tabulation dataset. If needed, the collection variable [DATESTCD]_DASCAT may be used to collect a category for each DATEST.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An internal or external identifier such as product label identifier.
Variables.Question Text: What is the [DATEST] product label identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record dispensed product label identifier.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. May be used to create RELREC to link this record with a record in EX domain.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The packaging identifier may be collected in different ways (e.g., affixing label onto CRF, scanning a bar code). For some cases, greater granularity for product identifiers may be needed. In this situation, applicants may need to use additional variables. This is an example of the type of collection variable names that can be used in a denormalized data structure.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date the study product was dispensed or returned, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the date [DATEST] product accountability was assessed?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the date product accountability was performed, using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable DADTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date study product dispensed/returned should be recorded for each dispensation for a study with multiple periods or multiple products dispensed. A single date may be collected when all observations are performed on the same date. The date of each observation can also be collected using the collection variable [DATESTCD]_DADAT. The date of the observation may be determined from a collected date of visit and in such cases a separate measurement date field is not required. This is an example the type of collection variable names that can be used in a denormalized data structure.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: DA Assessment Result in Original Units
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Result of the product accountability assessment (e.g., actual amount).
Variables.Question Text: What is the amount of the [DATEST] product accountability assessment?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the result of the product accountability assessment.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. In addition to the tabulation variable DAORRES, create DATESTCD from the collection variable name and derive the value of DATEST from DATESTCD. The prompt may also contain DATEST. Use appropriate CDISC Controlled Terminology for the test and test code.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Each test may be collected using the collection variable [TESTCD] (e.g., RETAMT) or [TESTCD]_DAORRES, where TESTCD is the appropriate CT for the DA test code (e.g., RETAMT_DAORRES). For a study with multiple periods or multiple products dispensed, accountability amounts should be assessed for each dispensation and return. For the tabulation dataset, DAREFID should be used to link related records. This is an example of the types of collection variable names that can be used in a denormalized data structure.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit of the result as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What was the unit of the [DATEST] result?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record or select the original units in which these data were collected, if not preprinted on CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The unit should be preprinted on the CRF or a field provided on the CRF to capture it. This is an example of the types of collection variable names that can be used in a denormalized data structure.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included in the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether a planned ECG measurement, series of ECG measurements, tests, or observations was performed.
Variables.Question Text: Was the ECG performed?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate whether or not an ECG or specific ECG test was done.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. May be used to derive a value into the tabulation variable EGSTAT. Variables.Implementation Notes: This may be implemented for an entire ECG, or a specific ECG test basis. General prompt question to be used as a data management tool to verify that missing results are confirmed missing.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The incidence number of a test that is repeated within a given timeframe for the same test. The level of granularity can vary (e.g., within a timepoint, within a visit; multiple measurements of blood pressure, multiple analyses of a sample).

Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record which repetition of the ECG this is.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An internal or external identifier of the ECG (e.g., waveform number).

(e.g., UUID for external waveform file, session number automatically generated by electronic equipment).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Method of the test or examination.
Variables.Question Text: What was the method used for the ECG?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the method used for the ECG.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes:
Results may be affected by whether conditions for ECG as specified in the protocol were properly met. One possible condition is the method used to collect or calculate the ECG data. If the protocol requires this type of information, then this question may be included to confirm that the method used matches the protocol. The following are examples of when it is not necessary to collect these data on the CRF: 
 * Method of ECG is provided as part of the electronic data. 
 * Method of ECG is not pertinent to the protocol. 
 * The protocol specifies only 1 possible method for collecting ECG measurements and the applicant does not feel there is significant risk of the sites performing the ECG using the incorrect method.

Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record which lead was used for this measurement.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This is used when more specificity for the location is desired for the ECG data.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The position of the subject during the ECG measurement.
Variables.Question Text: What was the position of the subject during the ECG measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the position of the subject during the ECG.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Results may be affected by whether conditions for ECG as specified in the protocol were properly met. If the protocol requires this type of information, then this question may be included to confirm that the subject's position matches the protocol. The following are examples of when it is not necessary to collect these data on the CRF:Position of the subject is provided as part of the electronic data.Position of the subject is not pertinent to the protocol.The protocol specifies only 1 possible position and the applicant does not feel there is significant risk of the sites performing the ECG with the subject in the wrong position.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date the ECG was performed, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the date of the ECG?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the date ECG was done using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable EGDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A complete date is expected. The date of collection may be determined from the date of visit (VISDAT) and if so, a separate assessment date field is not required.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A text description of planned time point when measurements should be taken as defined in the protocol.
Variables.Question Text: What was the planned time point of the ECG measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the time point labels for when the ECG test should be taken, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. Tabulation time-point anchors EGTPTREF (text description) and EGRFTDTC (date/time) may be needed, as well as tabulation variables EGTPTNUM, EGELTM.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Planned time points are needed to differentiate multiple sequential assessments. It is recommended that time points should be preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a free-text field. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Planned Time Point" can be included as the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Time of ECG, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the time the ECG was collected?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the time the ECG was done (as complete as possible).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable EGDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be required when multiple assessments are done on 1 day or when the timing in relationship to study product is required for analysis.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Descriptive name of the measurement or finding.
Variables.Question Text: What was the ECG test name?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the name of the ECG measurement or finding, if not preprinted on the CRF. If collected on the CRF, the applicant may provide additional instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the column with the heading Tabulation Target. The tabulation variable EGTESTCD may be determined from the value collected in EGTEST. The tabulation variables EGTESTCD and EGTEST are required in the tabulation datasets. Use appropriate CDISC Controlled Terminology for the test and test code.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Required to identify which test the result is for. It is recommended that the test names be preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a free-text field. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Test" can be included as the column heading.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: ECG Result or Finding in Original Units
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Result of the measurement or finding as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What was the result of the ECG?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record test results, interpretations or findings.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Both quantitative results and interpretive findings or summaries may be recorded here.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit of the result as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What was the unit of the ECG results?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record or select the original unit in which these data were collected, if not preprinted on CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be included if quantitative results are recorded. Because units for quantitative ECG results are typically limited, units should be preprinted on the CRF with the associated test when possible, rather than having sites record the units. This item is not necessary for qualitative results.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether the ECG results were clinically significant.
Variables.Question Text: Was the ECG clinically significant?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether ECG results were clinically significant.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPEG dataset as the value of SUPPEG.QVAL where SUPPEG.QNAM ="EGCLSIG" and SUPPEG.QLABEL="Clinically Significant".
Variables.Implementation Notes: Could apply to specific measurements or to overall interpretation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included in the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system-generated. This collection variable is typically collected in all domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The name of an encounter that encompasses planned and unplanned study interventions, procedures, and assessments that may be performed on a subject.
Variables.Question Text: What is the visit name?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The name of the clinical encounter is typically preprinted on the CRF or displayed in the EDC for any visit-based data collection, most often in Findings domains. This Visit text description is then available in any EDC data extract for that Findings domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Date the encounter occurred (or started).
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the date of the visit?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the [date/start date] of the visit using DD-MON-YYYY format.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field is not a tabulation variable. The date of a measurement, test, observation, or specimen collection can be determined from the date/time of visit (VISDAT/VISTIM) and then concatenating the VISDAT/VISTIM components and populating the tabulation variable LBDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date the laboratory specimens were collected can be determined from the visit date variable (VISDAT) and applying that date to all of the laboratory tests at that visit, or the specimen collection date can be collected on the Laboratory CRF using the date (LBDAT) field.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether a planned lab measurement, series of lab measurements, tests, observations or was performed or specimens collected.
Variables.Question Text: Was the sample collected?; Was the lab performed?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate whether or not lab specimen was collected or measurement performed.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. May be used to derive a value into the tabulation variable LBSTAT. If the collection variable LBPERF = "N", the value of LBSTAT will be "NOT DONE". If LBPERF = "Y", LBSTAT should be null. A combination of tabulation variables ( e.g., LBCAT and LBSCAT, LBTPT) is used to indicate that multiple tests were not done. In this situation, the tabulation variable LBTESTCD would be populated as LBALL and an appropriate test name (LBTEST) provided.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This may be implemented for an entire lab panel, or a specific lab test. General prompt question to be used as a data management tool to verify that missing results are confirmed missing.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date of specimen collection, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the (start) date of the lab specimen collection?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the (start) date when specimen collection was done using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable LBDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A complete date is expected. The date of specimen collection may be determined from the date of visit (VISDAT) and, if so, a separate assessment date field is not required. The tabulation LBDTC variable contains either a date/time when a specimen is collected at a point in time or the start date/time, when a specimen is collected over time.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The time of specimen collection, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the (start) time of the lab specimen collection?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the (start) time of collection (as complete as possible).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable LBDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be required when multiple assessments are done on 1 day or when the timing in relationship to study product is required for analysis or a specimen is collected over an extended time period.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the name of the lab panel?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the lab test category, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, and not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Category" can be included in the column heading. Laboratory tests have commonly recognized categories and subcategories that should be used whenever appropriate. LBCAT and or LBSCAT should be included if lab status (NOT DONE) is collected for each lab category/subcategory (e.g., HEMATOLOGY, CHEMISTRY, URINALYSIS).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the LBCAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the name of the lab sub-panel?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the lab test subcategory, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology (e.g. electrolytes, liver function). This would most commonly be preprinted on the CRF or screen and prepopulated in the data management system. This is not typically a question to which the site would provide an answer. Laboratory tests have commonly recognized categories and subcategories that should be used whenever appropriate. LBSCAT can only be used if there is an LBCAT, and it must be a subcategorization of LBCAT.

Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be submitted in a SUPPLB dataset as the value of SUPPLB.QVAL where SUPPLB.QNAM ="LBCOND" and SUPPLB.LABEL="Test Condition Met".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This information is collected when the laboratory test results may be affected by whether conditions for testing were properly met. The specific testing conditions required should be preprinted on the CRF. This may not be relevant for all tests.

Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Results may be affected by whether the subject was fasting. This may not be relevant for all tests.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An internal or external identifier (e.g., specimen identifier).
