Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. May be used to derive a value into the tabulation variable LBSTAT. If the collection variable LBPERF = "N", the value of LBSTAT will be "NOT DONE". If LBPERF = "Y", LBSTAT should be null. A combination of tabulation variables (e.g., LBCAT and LBSCAT, LBTPT) is used to indicate that multiple tests were not done. In this situation, the tabulation variable LBTESTCD would be populated as LBALL and an appropriate test name (LBTEST) provided.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This may be implemented for an entire panel, or on a specific test basis. General prompt question to be used as a data management tool to verify that missing results are confirmed missing.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date of specimen collection, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the (start) date of the lab specimen collection?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the (start) date of specimen collection using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable LBDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A complete date is expected. The date of collection may be determined from the date of visit (VISDAT) and, if so, a separate assessment date field is not required. The tabulation LBDTC variable contains either a date/time when a specimen is collected at a point in time or the start date/time, when a specimen is collected over time.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The time of specimen collection, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the (start) time of the lab specimen collection?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the (start) time of collection (as complete as possible)
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable LBDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be required when multiple assessments are done on 1 day or when the timing in relationship to study product is required for analysis or a specimen is collected over an extended time period.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the name of the lab panel?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the lab test category, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, and not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Category" can be included as the column heading. Laboratory tests have commonly recognized categories and subcategories that should be used whenever appropriate. LBCAT and or LBSCAT should be included if lab status (NOT DONE) is collected for each lab category (e.g., HEMATOLOGY, CHEMISTRY, URINALYSIS).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the LBCAT values based on user defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the name of the lab sub-panel?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the lab test subcategory, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, and not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Subcategory" can be included as the column heading. Laboratory tests have commonly recognized categories and subcategories that should be used whenever appropriate. LBSCAT can only be used if there is an LBCAT, and it must be a subcategorization of LBCAT.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A text description of planned time point when measurements should be taken as defined in the protocol.
Variables.Question Text: What was the planned time point of the lab?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the planned time-point labels for the lab test, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. Tabulation time-point anchors LBTPTREF (text description) and LBRFTDTC (date/time) may be needed, as well as tabulation variables LBTPTNUM, LBELTM.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Planned time points are needed to differentiate multiple sequential assessments. It is recommended that time points be preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a free-text field. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Planned Time Point" can be included as the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication that the subject has abstained from food/water for the specified amount of time.
Variables.Question Text: Was the subject fasting?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether the subject was fasting prior to the test being performed.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Results may be affected by whether the subject was fasting. This may not be relevant for all tests.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Indication of whether the testing conditions defined in the protocol were met
Variables.Question Text: Were the protocol-defined testing conditions met?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether protocol-defined testing conditions were met.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be submitted in a SUPPLB dataset as the value of SUPPLB.QVAL where SUPPLB.QNAM = "LBCOND" and SUPPLB.LABEL="Test Condition Met".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This information is collected when the laboratory test results may be affected by whether conditions for testing were properly met. The specific testing conditions required should be preprinted on the CRF This may not be relevant for all tests.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Description of the condition of the specimen.
Variables.Question Text: What was the condition of the specimen?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the condition of specimen.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be collected using free or standardized text. Results may be affected by whether conditions for specimen were properly met. When local processing is used, applicants may not routinely collect specimen condition.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Descriptive name of the lab test or examination used to obtain the measurement or finding. Any test normally performed by a clinical laboratory is considered a lab test.
Variables.Question Text: What was the lab test name?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the name of the lab measurement or finding, if not preprinted on the CRF. If collected on the CRF, the applicant may provide additional instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation variable LBTESTCD may be determined from the value collected in LBTEST. The tabulation variables LBTESTCD and LBTEST are required in the tabulation datasets. Use appropriate CDISC Controlled Terminology for the test and test code.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Required to identify which test the result is for. It is recommended that the test names be preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a free-text field that requires the site to enter text. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Test" can be included as the column heading.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: Lab Result or Finding in Original Units
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Result of the measurement or finding as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What was the result of the lab test?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the laboratory test result.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Both quantitative results and interpretive findings or summaries may be recorded here.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: Lab Method of Test or Examination
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Method of the test or examination.
Variables.Question Text: What was the method used for the lab test or examination?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the method of test or examination.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This information may be collected when more than 1 method is possible, and collecting the method used is necessary.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit of the result as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What was the unit of the lab result?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record or select the original unit in which these data were collected, if not preprinted on CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Should be preprinted on the CRF with the associated test when possible, rather than collected in a free-text field. Should be included if applicable and not available elsewhere. For some lab tests the units may not be applicable (e.g., urine color).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit of the result as originally received if it were collected as a non-standard unit.
Variables.Question Text: What was the unit of the lab result?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record or select the original unit in which these data were collected, if not preprinted on CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. The collected, nonstandard unit(s) may be submitted in a supplemental qualifier dataset.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The collected, nonstandard unit(s) should be reported as an equivalent standard unit in LBORRESU.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The toxicity grade, using a standard toxicity scale (e.g., NCI CTCAE).
Variables.Question Text: What is the toxicity grade?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the toxicity grade.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This is commonly used in oncology studies, but applicants may not collect these toxicity grades on CRFs. Terminology codelists (TOXGRV3, TOXGRV4) are available for use.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A description of toxicity quantified by LBTOXGR (e.g., NCI CTCAE Short Name).
Variables.Question Text: What is the description of the toxicity?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the description of the toxicity.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This would typically be the text description quantified by LBTOXGR (e.g., HYPERCALCEMIA, HYPOCALCEMIA)

Variables.Collection Variable Label: Lab Ref Range Lower Limit in Orig Unit
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The lower end of normal range or reference range for continuous results stored in LBORRES.
Variables.Question Text: What was the lower limit of the reference range for this lab test?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the lower limit of the reference range of the lab test.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: LBORNRLO and LBORNRHI should be populated only for continuous results; LBSTNRC should be populated only for non-continuous results. These data may be obtained from the lab or the electronic equipment. These data could be determined from a site or lab specific set of normal ranges stored in a look-up table.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: Lab Ref Range Upper Limit in Orig Unit
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The upper end of normal range or reference range for continuous results stored in LBORRES.
Variables.Question Text: What was the high limit of the reference range for this lab test?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the upper limit of the reference range of the lab test.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: LBORNRLO and LBORNRHI should be populated only for continuous results; LBSTNRC should be populated only for non-continuous results. These data may be obtained from the lab or the electronic equipment. These data could be determined from a site or lab specific set of normal ranges stored in a look-up table.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication or description of how the value compares to the normal range or reference range.
Variables.Question Text: How [did/do] the reported values compare within the [reference/normal/expected] range?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record where the lab result fell with respect to the reference range (e.g. HIGH, LOW, ABNORMAL).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Reference ranges may be defined by LBORNRLO and LBORNRHI or other objective criteria. Typically for local processing, "Reference Range Indicator" may be derived or determined programmatically and is not collected on the CRF. Should not be used to indicate clinical significance.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication whether lab test results were clinically significant.
Variables.Question Text: Was this result clinically significant?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether lab results were clinically significant.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be submitted in a SUPPLB dataset as the value of SUPPLB.QVAL where SUPPLB.QNAM= "LBCLSIG" and SUPPLB.QLABEL="Clinically Significant".
Variables.Implementation Notes: May be included if required by the protocol.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The name or identifier of the vendor (e.g., laboratory) that provided the test results.
Variables.Question Text: What was the name of the laboratory used?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the laboratory name.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Recommended to collect on the CRF if lab name was not collected at the site/study level or if multiple labs are used by a site.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included in the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system-generated. This collection variable is typically collected in all collection domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The name of an encounter that encompasses planned and unplanned study interventions, procedures, and assessments that may be performed on a subject.
Variables.Question Text: What is the visit name?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The name of the clinical encounter is typically preprinted on the CRF or displayed within the EDC for any visit-based data collection, most often in Findings domains. This Visit text description is then available in any EDC data extract for that Findings domain.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Date the encounter occurred (or started).
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the date of the visit?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the [date/start date] of the visit using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field is not a tabulation variable. The date of a measurement, test, observation can be determined from the date/time of visit (VISDAT/VISTIM) and then concatenating the VISDAT/VISTIM components and populating the tabulation variable PCDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date the PK samples were collected can be determined from the visit date variable (VISDAT) and applying that date to all of the PK samples at that visit, or the collection date can be collected on the PK CRF using the date (PCDAT) field.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether PK samples were collected.
Variables.Question Text: Were PK samples collected?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Check "No" if none of the samples were collected.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. May be used to derive a value into the tabulation variable PCSTAT. If PCPERF="N", the value of PCSTAT will be "NOT DONE". If PCPERF="Y", PCSTAT should be null. PCTEST and PCTESTCD must reflect what tests were not done. A combination of tabulation variables ( e.g., PCCAT and PCSCAT, PCTPT) is used to indicate that multiple tests were not done. In this situation, the tabulation variable PCTESTCD would be populated as PCALL and an appropriate test name (PCTEST) provided.
Variables.Implementation Notes: General prompt question to be used as a data management tool to verify that missing results are confirmed missing. This may be implemented at form level or sample level. These may be all samples of a particular type or all samples taken for some purpose and may need to be identified by the organization of the data on the form. Each sample collected could result in 1 or more tests performed, so there can be a one-to-one or one-to-many relationship between samples and tests/results.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: This variable used to indicate that data are not available, by having the site record the value as "Not Done".
Variables.Question Text: Record "Not Done" if the PK sample was not collected.
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the specimen was not done.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A Not Done checkbox, which indicates the test was "NOT DONE". Typically, there would be 1 checkbox for each measurement. This field can be useful on individual sample collections to confirm that a blank result field is meant to be blank.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An explanation for why the data are not available.
Variables.Question Text: What was the reason the PK sample was not collected?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Provide the reason why a PK sample was not collected.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The reason the data are not available may be chosen from an applicant-defined list (e.g., broken equipment, subject refused) or entered as free text. When PCREASND is used, the tabulation variable PCSTAT should also be populated in the tabulation dataset.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date of PK sample collection or the start date of PK sample collection over a period of time (protocol-defined time-point range), represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the date of the PK sample collection?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the date when PK sample collection occurred using this format (DD-MON-YYYY). If left blank, "PCDATFL" for this specimen must be populated (or "PCPERF" must be flagged to indicate this sample was not collected).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable PCDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A complete date is expected. The date of collection may be determined from the date of visit (VISDAT); if so, a separate assessment date field is not required. The tabulation PCDTC variable contains either a date/time when a specimen is collected at a point in time or the start date/time, when a specimen is collected over time.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Flag indicating that the PK date (or start date) is the same as the previous specimen collection date (or start date).
Variables.Question Text: Was the specimen/sample collected on the same date as the [last/previous specimen/sample] [collected/collection ended]?
Variables.Prompt: Same as Previous (Specimen/Sample Collection End) Date
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Select when the date of this specimen collection is the same as the date of the previous specimen collected. If left blank, "PCDAT" for this specimen must be populated. (or "PCPERF" must be flagged to indicate this sample was not collected)
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Does not map to a tabulation variable.
Variables.Implementation Notes: When a series of specimens are collected on a single form, this field is tied to the collection date to allow for the flag to be used as a surrogate for the date field. Its selection means that the date of this specimen is the same as the date of the last specimen collected (in the series). This variable may be used when collecting PK data and re-entering dates is more cumbersome than selecting the checkbox.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The time of PK sample collection or start time for a specimen collected over a period of time (protocol-defined time-point range), represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the time of the PK sample collection?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record time of collection (as complete as possible).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable PCDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A complete time is expected. The tabulation PCDTC variable contains either a date/time, when a specimen is collected at a point in time, or the start date/time, when a specimen is collected over time.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.Collection Variable Label: PK Sampling Planned Time Point Name
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A text description of planned timepoints when measurements should be taken, as defined in the protocol.
Variables.Question Text: What was the planned timepoint of the PK sample collection?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the planned time-point labels for the PK sample collection, if not preprinted on the CRF. Note: Planned timepoints are often described as relative to exposure to study product.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation time-point anchors PCTPTREF (text description) and PCRFTDTC (date/time) may be needed, as well as tabulation variables PCTPTNUM, PCELTM.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Planned timepoints are needed to differentiate multiple sequential assessments. It is recommended that timepoints should be preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a free-text field. If the form is laid out as a grid, then terms such as "Planned Time Point" can be included in the column heading.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Indication of whether the testing conditions defined in the protocol were met.
Variables.Question Text: Were the protocol-defined testing conditions met?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether protocol-defined testing conditions were met.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPPC dataset as the value of SUPPPC.QVAL where SUPPPC.QNAM ="PCCOND" and SUPP.PCLABEL= "Test Condition Met".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This information is collected when the test results may be affected by whether conditions for testing were properly met. The specific testing conditions required should be preprinted on the CRF. This may not be relevant for all tests.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An internal or external identifier (e.g., specimen identifier).
Variables.Question Text: What was the (PK) [reference identifier/accession number]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the specimen or accession number assigned.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. May be used to create RELREC to link this record with a record in another domain.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This can be used to reconcile CRF data. May be included for linking back to specimens (e.g., Specimen ID).

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The type of specimen used for a PK sample.
Variables.Question Text: What was the specimen (material) type?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the specimen material type, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The type of specimen used for a measure. Should be collected if not available elsewhere, or if required to differentiate multiple specimens.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Descriptive name of the analyte or specimen characteristics used to obtain the PK measurement or finding.
Variables.Question Text: What was the test name?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the name of the measurement or finding, if not preprinted on the CRF. If collected on the CRF, the applicant may provide additional instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation variable PCTESTCD may be determined from the value collected in PCTEST. The tabulation variables PCTESTCD and PCTEST are required in the tabulation datasets. Use appropriate CDISC Controlled Terminology for the test and test code.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicants typically collect tests related to the specimen characteristics on the CRF (e.g., Volume, Ph). Results for tests on an analyte (e.g., Concentration) would typically be populated when creating tabulation datasets. If the analyte test results are collected on the CRF, the test would be the analyte name. It is recommended that the test names be preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a free-text field. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Test" can be included in the column heading.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.Collection Variable Label: PK Sampling Result in Original Units
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Result of the measurement or finding as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What was the result of the test?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the test result, interpretation, or finding.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Should be preprinted on the CRF with the associated test when possible, rather than collected in a free-text field.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection at Fixed Time Points
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit of the result as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What was the unit of the result?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Select the original unit in which these data were collected, or record if not preprinted on CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Should be preprinted on the CRF with the associated test when possible, rather than collected in a free-text field.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included in the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study
Variables.Question Text: What is the subject identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system-generated. This collection variable is typically collected in all domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The name of an encounter that encompasses planned and unplanned study interventions, procedures, and assessments that may be performed on a subject.
Variables.Question Text: What is the visit name?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The name of the clinical encounter is typically preprinted on the CRF or displayed within the EDC for any visit-based data collection, most often in Findings domains. This Visit text description is then available in any EDC data extract for that Findings domain.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Date the encounter occurred (or started)
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the date of the visit?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the [date/start date] of the visit using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field is not a tabulation variable. The date of a measurement, test, or observation can be determined from the date/time of visit (VISDAT/VISTIM) and then concatenating the VISDAT/VISTIM components and populating the tabulation variable PCDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date the PK samples were collected can be determined from the visit date variable (VISDAT) and applying that date to all of the PK samples at that visit, or the collection date can be collected on the PK CRF using the date (PCDAT) field.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether PK samples were collected
Variables.Question Text: Were PK samples collected?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate whether all of the PK samples in this group were collected.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. May be used to derive a value into the tabulation variable PCSTAT. If PCPERF="N", the value of PCSTAT will be "NOT DONE". If PCPERF="Y", PCSTAT should be null. PCTEST and PCTESTCD must reflect what tests were not done. A combination of tabulation variables (e.g., PCCAT and PCSCAT, PCTPT) is used to indicate that multiple tests were not done. In this situation, the tabulation variable PCTESTCD would be populated as PCALL and an appropriate test name (PCTEST) provided.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This general prompt question is used as a data management tool to verify that missing results are confirmed missing. This may be implemented at form level or sample level. These may be all samples of a particular type, or all samples taken for some purpose, and may need to be identified by the organization of the data on the form. Each sample collected could result in 1 or more tests performed, so there can be a one-to-one or one-to-many relationship between samples and tests/results.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An explanation for why the data are not available
Variables.Question Text: What was the reason the PK sample was not collected?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Provide the reason why a PK sample was not collected.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The reason the data are not available may be chosen from an applicant-defined list (e.g., broken equipment, subject refused) or entered as free text. When PCREASND is used, the tabulation variable PCSTAT should also be populated in the tabulation dataset.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date of PK sample collection or the start date of PK sample collection over a period of time (protocol-defined time-point range), represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY)
Variables.Question Text: What was the date of the PK sample collection?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the date when PK sample collection occurred using this format (DD-MON-YYYY). If left blank, "PCDATFL" for this specimen must be populated (or "PCPERF" must be flagged to indicate this sample was not collected).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable PCDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A complete date is expected. The tabulation PCDTC variable contains either a date/time when a specimen is collected at a point in time or the start date/time, when a specimen is collected over time.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The time of PK sample collection or start time for a specimen collected over a period of time (protocol-defined time-point range), represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss)
Variables.Question Text: What was the start time of the PK sample collection?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record start time of collection (as complete as possible).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable PCDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A complete time is expected. In interval collection, start can be added as needed to the question text, prompt and CRF directions. The tabulation PCDTC variable contains either a date/time when a specimen is collected at a point in time or the start date/time, when a specimen is collected over time.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The end date of the specimen collection, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY)
Variables.Question Text: What was the end date of the specimen collection?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the date when PK sample collection stopped using this format (DD-MON-YYYY)
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected END DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable PCENDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The end date of specimen collection may be determined from the date of visit and if so, a separate assessment date field is not required.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The end time of the specimen collection, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss)
Variables.Question Text: What was the specimen collection end time?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record end time of collection (as complete as possible).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected END DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable PCENDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A complete end time is expected. The tabulation variable PCENDTC variable contains the end date/time, when a specimen is collected over time. If there is no end date/time, the tabulation variable PCENDTC should be Null.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.Collection Variable Label: PK Sampling Planned Time Point Name
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A text description of planned timepoints when measurements should be taken, as defined in the protocol
Variables.Question Text: What was the planned timepoint of the PK sample collection?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the planned time-point labels for the PK sample collection, if not preprinted on the CRF. Note: Planned timepoints are often described as relative to exposure to study product.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation time-point anchors PCTPTREF (text description) and PCRFTDTC (date/time) may be needed, as well as tabulation variables PCTPTNUM, PCELTM.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Planned timepoints are needed to differentiate multiple sequential assessments. It is recommended that timepoints should be preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a free-text field. If the form is laid out as a grid, then terms such as "Planned Time Point" can be included in the column heading.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication that the subject has abstained from food/water for the specified amount of time
Variables.Question Text: Was the subject fasting?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether the subject was fasting prior to the test being performed.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: To be used when results may be affected by whether the subject was fasting.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Indication of whether the testing conditions defined in the protocol were met (e.g., low fat diet)
Variables.Question Text: Were the protocol-defined testing conditions met?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether protocol-defined testing conditions were met.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPPC dataset as the value of SUPPPC.QVAL where SUPPPC.QNAM ="PCCOND" and SUPP.PCLABEL= "Test Condition Met".
Variables.Implementation Notes: This information is collected when the test results may be affected by whether conditions for testing were properly met. The specific testing conditions required should be preprinted on the CRF. This may not be relevant for all tests.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An internal or external identifier (e.g., specimen identifier)
Variables.Question Text: What was the (PK) [reference identifier/accession number]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the specimen or accession number assigned.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. May be used to create RELREC to link this record with a record in another domain.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This can be used to reconcile CRF data. May be included for linking back to specimens (e.g., Specimen ID).

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The type of specimen used for a PK sample
Variables.Question Text: What was the specimen (material) type?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the specimen material type, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The type of specimen used for a measure. Should be collected if not available elsewhere, or if required to differentiate multiple specimens.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Descriptive name of the analyte or specimen characteristics used to obtain the PK measurement or finding
Variables.Question Text: What was the test name?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the name of the measurement or finding, if not preprinted on the CRF. If collected on the CRF, the applicant may provide additional instructions to ensure the data is entered as intended.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation variable PCTESTCD may be determined from the value collected in PCTEST. The tabulation variables PCTESTCD and PCTEST are required in the tabulation datasets. Use appropriate CDISC Controlled Terminology for the test and test code.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicants typically collect tests related to the specimen characteristics on the CRF (e.g., Volume, pH). Results for tests on an analyte (e.g., Concentration) would typically be populated when the tabulation datasets are created. If analyte test results are collected on the CRF, the test would be the analyte name. It is recommended that test names be preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a free-text field. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Test" can be included in the column heading.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.Collection Variable Label: PK Sampling Result in Original Units
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Result of the measurement or finding as originally received or collected
Variables.Question Text: What was the result of the test?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the PK sampling test result.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Both quantitative results and interpretive findings or summaries may be recorded here.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: PK Sample Collection over a Time Interval
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit of the result as originally received or collected
Variables.Question Text: What was the unit of the result?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the PK sampling test result.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Both quantitative results and interpretive findings or summaries may be recorded here.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included in the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system-generated. This collection variable is typically collected in all collection domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The name of an encounter that encompasses planned and unplanned study interventions, procedures, and assessments that may be performed on a subject.
Variables.Question Text: What is the visit name?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This collection variable is typically collected in all collection domains. However, this collection variable is represented only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Date the encounter occurred (or started).
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the date of the visit?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the [date/start date] of the visit using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field is not a tabulation variable. The date of a measurement, test, observation can be determined from the date/time of visit (VISDAT/VISTIM) and then concatenating the collection VISDAT/VISTIM components and populating the tabulation variable SCDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date the subject characteristics were collected can be determined from the visit date variable (VISDAT) and applying that date to all of the subject characteristics at that visit, or the collection date can be included on the SC CRF using the date (SCDAT) field.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the category of the subject characteristics??
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the subject characteristics category, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Category" can be included in the column heading. This is an example of the types of collection variable names that can be used in a denormalized data structure.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the SCCAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the subcategory of the subject characteristics?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the subject characteristics subcategory, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Subcategory" can be included in the column header. SCSCAT can only be used if there is an SCCAT, and it must be a subcategorization of SCCAT. This is an example of the types of collection variable names that can be used in a denormalized data structure.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether any subject characteristics were collected.
Variables.Question Text: Were subject characteristics collected for [SCTESTCD]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if subject characteristics information was collected. If Yes, include the appropriate details where indicated on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. May be used to derive a value into the tabulation variable SCSTAT. If [SCTESTCD]_SCPERF ="N", the value of SCSTAT will be "NOT DONE". If [SCTESTCD]_SCPERF ="Y", SCSTAT should be null. A combination of tabulation variables (e.g., SCCAT and SCSCAT, SCTPT ) is used to indicate that multiple tests were not done. In this situation, the tabulation variable SCTESTCD would be assigned SCALL and an appropriate test name ( SCTEST) provided.
Variables.Implementation Notes: General prompt question to be used as a data management tool to verify that missing results are confirmed missing. This may be implemented for all tests collected on the same horizontal record or for each specific test. When the tabulation datasets are created, the value of SCPERF would apply to all tests on the same record. Use the collection variable [SCTESTCD]_SCPERF when implemented on a specific test basis. This is an example of the types of collection variable names that can be used in a denormalized data structure.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An applicant-defined identifier used to tie together a block of related records in a single domain.
Variables.Question Text: What is the test group identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record unique group identifier. Applicants may insert additional instructions to ensure each record has a unique group identifier.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: It can be beneficial to use an identifier in a data query to communicate clearly to the site the specific record in question. This group identifier ties together all the tests collected on this horizontal record. This field may be populated by the applicant's data collection system.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: SC Result or Finding in Original Units
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Result of the subject characteristics as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What is the subject's [SCTEST]?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the subject characteristic.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the study identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Although this field is not typically captured on a CRF, it should be displayed clearly on the CRF and/or in the EDC system. This field can be included in the database or populated during tabulation dataset creation.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique identifier for a site within a study.
Variables.Question Text: What is the site identifier?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically preprinted in the header of each CRF page for single-site studies. For studies with multiple sites, this field may be left blank so that the number can be recorded by the site, or it may be preprinted on the CRFs that are shipped to each site. \n EDC: This should be prepopulated.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A unique subject identifier within a site and a study.
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the (study) [subject/participant] identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the identifier for the subject.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Paper: This is typically recorded in the header of each CRF page. EDC: The subject identifiers may be system-generated. This collection variable is typically collected in all colelction domains. However, this collection variable is populated only in the tabulation DM domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The name of an encounter that encompasses planned and unplanned study interventions, procedures, and assessments that may be performed on a subject.
Variables.Question Text: What is the visit name?
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The name of the clinical encounter is typically preprinted on the CRF or displayed within the EDC for any visit-based data collection, most often in Findings domains. This Visit text description is then available in any EDC data extract for that Findings domain.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Date the encounter occurred (or started).
Variables.Question Text: What [is/was] the date of the visit?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the [date/start date] of the visit using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This field is not a tabulation variable. The date of a measurement, test, observation can be determined from the date/time of visit (VISDAT/VISTIM) and then concatenating the VISDAT/VISTIM components and populating the tabulation variable VSDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: The date the VS measurements were collected can be determined from the visit date variable (VISDAT) and applying that date to all of the observations at that visit, or the collection date can be included on the VS CRF using the date field (VSDAT).

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether a planned vital signs measurement, series of vital signs measurements, tests, or observations was performed.
Variables.Question Text: Were [vital signs/[VSTEST] performed?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the vital signs were collected. If Yes, include the appropriate details where indicated on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. May be used to derive a value into the tabulation variable VSSTAT. If VSPERF="N", the value of VSSTAT will be "NOT DONE". If VSPERF="Y", VSSTAT should be null. A combination of tabulation variables (e.g., VSCAT and VSSCAT, VSTPT) is used to indicate that multiple tests were not done. In this situation, the tabulation variable VSTESTCD would be populated as VSALL and an appropriate test name (VSTEST) provided.
Variables.Implementation Notes: This general prompt question is used as a data management tool to verify that missing results are confirmed missing. This may be implemented for all tests collected on the same horizontal record or for each specific test. When mapped to the tabulation dataset, the value of VSPERF would apply to all tests on the same record. Use the collection variable [VSTESTCD]_VSPERF when implemented on a specific test basis.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The date of the vital signs measurement, represented in an unambiguous date format (e.g., DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Question Text: What was the date of the measurement(s)?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record date of measurements using this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable VSDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A single date may be collected for all the vital sign measurements when they are performed on the same date. The date of each measurement can also be collected for each measurement using a collection variable [VSTESTCD]_VSDAT. The date of the measurements may be determined from a collected date of visit; in such cases, a separate measurement date field is not required.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The time of measurement, represented in an unambiguous time format (e.g., hh:mm:ss).
Variables.Question Text: What was the time of the measurement(s)?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record time of measurement (as complete as possible).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable VSDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A single collection time (e.g., VSTIM) may be collected for all the measurements when they are performed at the same time. The time of each measurement can also be collected using a collection variable [VSTESTCD]_VSTIM.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A grouping of topic-variable values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the category of the vital signs?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the vital signs category, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be from an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Category" can be included in the column heading.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A sub-division of the VSCAT values based on user-defined characteristics.
Variables.Question Text: What was the subcategory of the vital signs?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the vital signs subcategory, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Applicant-defined controlled terminology. This would most commonly be either a heading or a preprinted category value on the CRF, not a question to which the site would provide an answer. If a question is asked, the response would typically be an applicant-defined codelist. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Subcategory" can be included in the column header. VSSCAT can only be used if there is a VSCAT, and it must be a subcategorization of VSCAT.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An applicant-defined identifier used to tie a block of related records in a single domain.
Variables.Question Text: What is the vital signs group identifier?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record unique group identifier. The applicant may insert additional instructions to ensure each record has a unique group identifier.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: It can be beneficial to use an identifier in a data query to communicate clearly to the site the specific record in question. This group identifier ties together all the tests collected on the same horizontal record. This field may be populated by the applicant's data collection system.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: Vital Signs Planned Time Point Name
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A text description of planned timepoints when measurements should be taken, as defined in the protocol.
Variables.Question Text: What is the planned timepoint for this vital signs measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the planned time-point labels for vital signs, if not preprinted on the CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. The tabulation time-point anchors VSTPTREF (text description) and VSRFTDTC (date/time) may be needed, as well as tabulation variables VSTPTNUM, VSELTM.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Planned timepoints are needed to differentiate multiple sequential assessments. It is recommended that timepoints should be preprinted on the CRF rather than collected in a free-text field. If the form is laid out as a grid, then words such as "Planned Time Point" can be included in the column heading. The planned timepoint of each measurement can also be collected using the collection variable [VSTESTCD]_VSTPT.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: This variable is used to indicate that data are not available, by having the site recording the value as "Not Done".
Variables.Question Text: Indicate if the [VSTEST] measurement was not done.
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Indicate if the vital signs measurement was not done.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A single "Not Done" can be collected once for all tests on the same horizontal record using VSSTAT. The value of VSSTAT applies to all measurements on that record when mapped to the tabulation dataset. If needed, for each test "NOT DONE" may be collected using the collection variable [VSTESTCD]_VSSTAT.

Variables.Collection Variable Label: VS Result or Finding in Original Units
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Result of the vital signs measurement as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What was the result of the [VSTEST] measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the vital sign results.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column. In addition to the tabulation variable VSORRES, create VSTESTCD from the collection variable name and determine the value of VSTEST from VSTESTCD. The prompt may also contain the VSTEST. Use appropriate CDISC Controlled Terminology for the test and test code.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Each test may be collected using the collection variable [TESTCD] e.g., SYSBP or [TESTCD]_VSORRES where TESTCD is the appropriate CT for the VS test code e.g., SYSBP_VSORRES. This is an examples of the types of collection variable names that can be used in a denormalized data structure.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The unit of the result as originally received or collected.
Variables.Question Text: What was the unit of the [VSTEST] measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record or select the original unit in which these data were collected, if not preprinted on CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: A single Unit field can be collected once for all measurements collected on the same horizontal record using VSUNIT. The value of VSUNIT applies to all measurements on that record when mapped to the tabulation dataset. If needed for each measurement, unit may be collected using the collection variable [VSTESTCD]_VSORRESU. Should be preprinted on the CRF (or enterable from a picklist) with the associated test when possible, rather than collected as free-text.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: An indication of whether the vital signs results were clinically significant.
Variables.Question Text: Was the [VSTEST] result clinically significant?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record whether the vital sign result was clinically significant.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to an tabulation variable. This information could be represented in a SUPPVS dataset as the value of SUPPVS.QVAL where SUPPVS.QNAM = "VSCLSIG" and SUPPVS.QLABEL="Clinically Significant".
Variables.Implementation Notes: In horizontal data collection, a collection variable [VSTESTCD]_VSCLSIG may be created for each VSTESTCD and added to the CRF if needed.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: The position of the subject during a measurement or examination.
Variables.Question Text: What was the position of the subject during the [VSTEST] measurement?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the position of subject at time of test (e.g. SITTING).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Results may be affected by whether conditions for vital signs as specified in the protocol were properly met. One common condition is the subject's position. If the protocol requires this type of information, then a collection variable [VSTESTCD]_VSPOS may be created for each VSTESTCD and added to the CRF, if needed.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A description of the anatomical location of the subject, relevant to the collection of vital signs measurements.
Variables.Question Text: What was the anatomical location where the [VSTEST] measurement was taken?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record or select location on body where measurement was performed, if not preprinted on CRF.
Variables.Mapping Instructions: Maps directly to the tabulation variable listed in the Tabulation Target column.
Variables.Implementation Notes: Collected or preprinted on the CRF when the applicant needs to identify the specific anatomical location (e.g., ARM for blood pressure). Applicants may collect the data using a subset list of controlled terminology on the CRF. In horizontal data collection, a collection variable [VSTESTCD]_VSLOC may be created for each VSTESTCD and added to the CRF, if needed. LAT, DIR, and PORTOT are used to further describe the anatomical location.

Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: Qualifier for anatomical location, further detailing the side of the body.

Variables.Data Collection Scenario/Implementation: Birth date collection using a single date field
Variables.DRAFT Collection Definition: A subject's date of birth (with or without the time of birth). The complete Date of Birth is made from the temporal components of Birth Year, Birth Month, Birth Day, and Birth Time..
Variables.Question Text: What is the subject's date of birth?
Variables.Case Report Form Completion Instructions: Record the date of birth to the level of precision known (e.g., day/month/year, year, month/year) in this format (DD-MON-YYYY).
Variables.Mapping Instructions: This does not map directly to a tabulation variable. For the tabulation dataset, concatenate all collected DATE and TIME components and populate the tabulation variable BRTHDTC in ISO 8601 format.
Variables.Implementation Notes: BRTHDAT is the collected field used for recording the full birth date. The applicant may choose to database the date of birth as a single variable (BRTHDAT), or as separate variables for each component of the date/time (BRTHYY, BRTHMO, BRTHDD, BRTHTIM). The applicant may choose a method based on database considerations, or for regulatory reasons. It is expected that what is collected for BRTHDAT (e.g., complete date, selected components) is reported in the tabulation variable BRTHDTC in ISO 8601 format. If data are collected in a manner resulting in a reduced precision level, then AGE, if not collected on the CRF, should be derived using a documented algorithm that describes how age was determined and/or imputed for those birth dates collected with reduced precision.
